keywords.name: Security A.
keywords.sum: <Security A.> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect will have a modified number of security checks according to the number specified for this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Security A. +1>.

keywords.name: Blocker
keywords.sum: <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")

keywords.name: Recovery
keywords.sum: <Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.

keywords.name: Piercing
keywords.sum: <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")

keywords.name: Draw
keywords.sum: <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.

keywords.name: Jamming
keywords.sum: <Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.

keywords.name: Digisorption
keywords.sum: <Digisorption> is a keyword effect. When a digivolution into a Digimon card with this effect in the hand would occur, by suspending 1 of your Digimon, the digivolution cost is reduced according to the value specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digisorption-3>.

keywords.name: Reboot
keywords.sum: <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.

keywords.name: De-Digivolve
keywords.sum: <De-Digivolve> is a keyword effect where the player declares a number from 1 up to the number specified in the effect, then the declared number of cards are trashed from the chosen stack(s) of cards starting with the top card. This is shown on cards using text such as <De - Digivolve 1>.

keywords.name: Retaliation
keywords.sum: <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.

keywords.name: Digi-Burst
keywords.sum: <Digi-Burst> is a keyword effect where another effect specified by this effect will activate by trashing the specified number of digivolution cards from the Digimon with this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digi-Burst 1>.

keywords.name: Rush
keywords.sum: <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.

keywords.name: Blitz
keywords.sum: <Blitz> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect can attack if your opponent has 1 or more memory.

keywords.name: Delay
keywords.sum: <Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.

keywords.name: Decoy
keywords.sum: <Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.

keywords.name: Armor Purge
keywords.sum: <Armor Purge> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with <Armor Purge> would be deleted, by trashing the top card of the Digimon with this effect, this effect prevents the deletion.

keywords.name: Save
keywords.sum: <Save> is a keyword effect that allows you to place this card under 1 of your Tamers.

keywords.name: Material Save
keywords.sum: <Material Save> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted, this effect allows you to place a number of the cards specified in the top card's DigiXros requirements from among the digivolution cards under 1 of your Tamers. The number of cards placed is the number specified in this keyword effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Material Save 1>.

keywords.name: Evade
keywords.sum: <Evade> is a keyword effect. By suspending a Digimon with this effect when it would be deleted, this effect prevents the deletion.

keywords.name: Raid
keywords.sum: <Raid> is a keyword effect that can switch the target of attack to the opponent's unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when a Digimon with this keyword effect attacks.

keywords.name: Alliance
keywords.sum: <Alliance> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack.

keywords.name: Barrier
keywords.sum: <Barrier> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle, by trashing the top card of your security stack, this effect prevents that deletion.

keywords.name: Blast Digivolve
keywords.sum: <Blast Digivolve> is a keyword effect that allows one of your Digimon to digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost.

keywords.name: Fortitude
keywords.sum: <Fortitude> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted, you play this Digimon without paying the cost.

keywords.name: Mind Link
keywords.sum: <Mind Link> is a keyword effect that places a Tamer with this effect in the digivolution cards of a Digimon with no Tamer cards in its digivolution cards.

keywords.name: Partition
keywords.sum: <Partition> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle, you may play 1 of each of the specified cards from the digivolution cards without paying their costs. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Partition (blue Lv.4 & green Lv.4)>."

keywords.name: Collision
keywords.sum: <Collision> is a keyword effect. While a Digimon with this effect is attacking, all of your opponent's Digimon gain <Blocker> and the opponent player is forced to block whenever possible during the block timing.

keywords.name: Blast DNA Digivolve
keywords.sum: <Blast DNA Digivolve> is a keyword effect. One of your Digimon specified in this effect and a card from your hand may digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Blast DNA Digivolve> <[Durandamon] + [BryweLudramon]>."

keywords.name: Scapegoat
keywords.sum: <Scapegoat> is a keyword effect. By deleting 1 of your other Digimon when a Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects, this effect prevents the deletion.

keywords.name: Vortex
keywords.sum: <Vortex> allows the Digimon with this effect to attack an opponent's Digimon at the end of your turn. <Vortex> is a keyword effect that also allows a Digimon to attack in the same turn it was played.

keywords.name: Overclock
keywords.sum: <Overclock> is a keyword effect. At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or 1 of your other specified Digimon, the Digimon with this effect attacks a player without suspending. This is shown on cards using text such as <Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)>.

keywords.name: Iceclad
keywords.sum: <Iceclad> is a keyword effect where you compare the number of digivolution cards instead of DP when you battle using the Digimon with this effect, other than battles against Security Digimon.

keywords.name: Decode
keywords.sum: <Decode> is a keyword effect. When the Digimon with this effect would leave the battle area other than by a battle, you may play 1 specified Digimon card from that Digimon's digivolution cards without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Decode (blue Lv.4)>."

keywords.name: Fragment
keywords.sum: <Fragment> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted, by choosing and trashing the specified number of this Digimon's digivolution cards, it isn't deleted. The effect is indicated on cards by icons such as <Fragment (3)>.

keywords.name: Execute
keywords.sum: <Execute> is a keyword effect. At the end of your turn, the Digimon with this keyword effect may attack. At the end of the attack, this Digimon is deleted. This effect also allows for attacking an opponent's unsuspended Digimon.

keywords.name: Progress
keywords.sum: <Progress> is a keyword effect that reads "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent's effects while attacking."

keywords.name: Link +
keywords.sum: <Link +> is a keyword effect that adds the specified number to the maximum link cards of the Digimon with this effect.

keywords.name: Training
keywords.sum: <Training> is a keyword effect that reads "By suspending this Digimon during the main phase, place the top card of your deck at the bottom of this Digimon's digivolution cards. This effect can also activate in the breeding area."

keywords.name: Use Req.
keywords.sum: <Use Req.> is a keyword effect that allows a player to ignore the color requirements with the specified cards.

keywords.name: Ascension
keywords.sum: <Ascension> is a keyword effect. When the card with this effect is deleted, the player may place this card at the top of the security stack.

keywords.name: Engage
keywords.sum: <Engage> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect may attack at the end of your turn.

keywords.name: Guard
keywords.sum: <Guard> is a keyword effect. When any of a player's other Digimon would leave the battle area by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, it doesn't leave.

keywords.name: Detach
keywords.sum: <Detach> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon would leave the battle area other than by your effects, by trashing 1 of its specified link cards, it doesn't leave." It is shown on cards using text such as "<Detach ([Seven Code] trait)>."

keywords.name: Succession
keywords.sum: <Succession> is a keyword effect that reads "This Digimon gains all effects other than <Succession> on its topmost specified digivolution card." It is shown on cards using text such as "<Succession ([Ceresmon])>."

rules.t: Game Overview
Number of Players
This game is played by two players in a match against each other.
Game Victory/Loss
When a player meets the victory conditions, they win the game.
The game will end when one of the players wins or loses.
Victory conditions

When an attack by your Digimon allows for 1 or more security checks, the attack is successful against your opponent, and your opponent has 0 security cards. (For details, refer to 11-5 "Confirming if an Attack is Successful")
Your opponent has 0 cards in their deck and can't draw a card during your opponent's draw phase.
At any point during the game, either player may declare that they forfeit. After a player declares a forfeit, they immediately lose the game.
A forfeit is never forced, and effects don't trigger or activate for loss by forfeit.
Some card effects can cause a player to win or lose the game. When such an effect is resolved, the player will win or lose.
Fundamental Principles

Any card text that conflicts with the Official Rules will be prioritized over the rules. (Example: A Digimon can't attack the turn it's played according to the rules, but a Digimon with <Rush> can attack by that effect.)

If a player is requested to perform an impossible action, that action will not be carried out. If only some of those actions are impossible, the player performs as many of the required actions as possible.

If a card in a given state is requested to be changed to that same state, the card remains in its current state. (Example: If a suspended Digimon is chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, the action of suspending it isn't performed.)

If processing is to be performed 0 or fewer times due to a rule or effect, that processing can't be performed. The opposite of the processing can't be performed, even if processing is to be performed a negative number of times.

If multiple players are simultaneously requested to make a choice due to a rule or effect, the turn player makes their choice first. After the turn player makes their choice, the non-turn player makes their choice.

When choosing cards by a rule or an effect, 1 or more cards must be chosen. You can't choose less than 1 card. (Example: "[Main] Choose any number of your opponent's Digimon whose total DP adds up to 8000 or less and delete all of them" would require you to choose at least 1 of your opponent's Digimon whose total DP adds up to 8000 or less.)
When a rule or effect modifies a numerical value, the result will always be an integer.

When a rule or effect modifies a numerical value multiple times, first the modifying value is calculated, then it's applied to the original value. (Example: If both a +3000 DP and-2000 DP are applied to 1 Digimon, the final modifying value of +1000 will be applied to that Digimon.)
Even if a cost to be paid becomes a negative value by a rule or effect, the final cost will not be a negative value.
When cards are to be shuffled by a rule or an effect, you must randomize the order of those cards. If a card to be shuffled is public, it is made private before shuffling.
Rules for Declaring Utilization of a Card

A player can declare they are utilizing a card (playing, digivolving, using, or linking) only if that card is able to be utilized. They can't declare its utilization if they can't pay its cost or alternate cost.

If processing conditions exist as part of an alternate cost, the player can declare that card only if the processing conditions are currently met and the alternate cost can be paid. (Example: If a card has a play cost of 12 and the effect "When this card would be played, if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer, reduce the cost by 5," then you can declare you are playing that card if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer and are able to pay the cost of 7.)

If optional processing conditions exist as part of an alternate cost, the player can declare that card only if those processing conditions are met and the alternate cost can be paid. Additionally, the player must perform as much of the processing as needed in order to pay the cost. (Example: If a card has a play cost of 11 and the effect "When this card would be played, by suspending 2 of your Digimon, reduce the cost by 4," and you have 2 Digimon that can be suspended and are able to pay the cost of 7, then you must suspend those 2 Digimon if you declare you are playing it.)

If a card has DigiXros or Assembly, the player can declare that card only if the alternate cost can be paid, including any immediate-type effects (triggered by the declaration of that card) which increase the areas that cards can be placed from. Additionally, the player must perform as much of the processing as needed in order to pay the cost.
Items Required for the Game
Deck and Digi-Egg deck
"Deck" and "Digi-Egg deck" refer to the decks composed of the cards used in the game.
Deck
A deck must have exactly 50 cards. It can't have more or less cards.
A deck can include up to 4 copies of a card with the same card number. However, this doesn't apply to rules or effects that place 4 or more cards.
Digi-Egg Deck
A Digi-Egg deck can have 5 or fewer cards. As long as it has 5 or fewer cards, it can have as many cards as you like, or even 0 cards.
A Digi-Egg deck can include up to 4 copies of a card with the same card number. However, this doesn't apply to rules or effects that place 4 or more cards.
The Memory Gauge
The memory gauge shows the numbers that represent the memory. One memory gauge is shared between both players during the game.

0 on the memory gauge is the center, and it has the numbers 1 through 10 on both the left and the right. The highest number on the memory gauge is 10 on both the left and the right. The memory won't exceed 10.
0 on the memory gauge is the center, the numbers on the left represent your memory, and the numbers on the right represent your opponent's memory.
Marker
The marker is used to indicate the current memory. One marker is shared between both players.
Token Cards

Token cards are non-game cards used by effects. You may prepare as many token cards as you like, but you must prepare token cards if your deck or Digi-Egg deck includes a card with an effect that uses tokens. (For details, refer to 4-21 "Tokens")
Token cards can't be included in a deck or Digi-Egg deck.
Token cards must be cards that can show their orientation. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")
When using token cards, players don't have to declare the effect to be used with the token in advance. However, the card information must be written on the token cards to be used.
A token card can be played even if its card information doesn't include a play cost.
Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules)
The Index is a card that shows the various keyword skills and rules for cards. You can bring as many copies of the Index as you like.
The Index can't be included in a deck or Digi-Egg deck.
The Index doesn't have any effect on games.
The Index can be confirmed at any point in a game.
Counter Markers (Dice)
Counter markers can be used to represent various things in the game. Players may bring any number of counter markers.
Card Information
If the card information varies on the same cards, the card information on the newest card is always referenced.
Card Category
This information indicates the card category for a card.
The card categories are Digi-Egg cards, Digimon cards, Tamer cards, and Option cards.
Digi-Egg cards are cards used for building Digi-Egg decks. These cards have "DIGI-EGG" written at the top edge of the card.
Digimon cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "DIGIMON" written at the top edge of the card.
Tamer cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "TAMER" written at the top edge of the card.
Option cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "OPTION" written at the top edge of the card.
Information Written on Cards
Name
The individual card name of the card.

When card information is specified in an effect only using brackets, only the cards that match the name shown in brackets can be referenced. (Example: An effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your [Marcus Damon] get +3000 DP and <Security Attack +1>" will give cards with the name [Marcus Damon] +3000 DP and <Security A. +1>.)
When text specifies "with [XX] in its name," cards whose names include the text in brackets can be referenced.
When a card has "ACE" written in its name, "ACE" is not included in the card name.
Traits
This information indicates multiple traits including form, attribute, and type.
If a single card has multiple traits, each trait will be separated by slashes.
When an effect specifies "with the [XX] trait," cards with the trait that matches the text in brackets can be referenced.
When an effect specifies "with [XX] in any of its traits," cards with one or more traits that include the text in brackets can be referenced.
Effects
An effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the upper text on a card. (For details, refer to 15-1 "Effects")
When a rule or effect references the "effect" part of card information, the upper text on a card is to be referenced.

If a rule or effect references a "persistent keyword effect" in card information, it references cards that always possess that keyword effect. (Example: An effect that specifies a card with the <Blocker> effect references cards that always possess the <Blocker> effect and does not reference cards with effects that give <Blocker> and such.)

If a rule or effect references a "keyword effect that executes processing" in card information, it references cards that do not involve processing conditions or optional processing conditions in the activation of that keyword effect. (Example: An effect that specifies cards with the <Blitz> effect references cards that do not involve processing conditions such as "if," "while," or "by" in the activation of that <Blitz> effect.)
(Rule)
The (Rule) icon is a rule specific to that card, not an effect. A (Rule) always applies.
(Rule) Trait: Has [XX].
A card with this (Rule) is treated as having the [XX] trait.
(Rule) Name: Also treated as [XX].
The name of a card with this (Rule) is also treated as [XX].
(Rule) Name: Also treated as having [XX].
A card with this (Rule) is treated as also having [XX] in its name. However, this rule doesn't treat that card as a card with the name [XX].
(Rule) Card number: Also treated as [XX].
The card number of a card with this (Rule) is also treated as [XX].
(Rule) A player can include up to X copies of cards with this card's card number in their deck.
When a card has this (Rule), up to X copies of that card can be included in a deck build.
Digivolution Requirements
This indicates information regarding the possible card for digivolution and the digivolution cost required.
A digivolution cost is the cost required to digivolve into that Digimon card. (For details, refer to 8-1 "Digivolving")

Text after the [Digivolve] icon or "Digivolve:" is also included in the digivolution requirements of such cards. (Example: A card with "[Digivolve] [Koromon]: Cost 0" can digivolve from a card named [Koromon] for a cost of 0.)
DNA Digivolution
The digivolution requirements for DNA digivolution. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")
The explanation for DNA digivolution is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
DigiXros Requirements
The requirements for a DigiXros. (For details, refer to 7-2 "DigiXros")
The explanation for DigiXros requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
Burst Digivolve
The digivolution requirements for burst digivolve. (For details, refer to 8-3 "Burst Digivolve")
The explanation for burst digivolve is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
App Fusion
The digivolution requirements for App Fusion. (For details, refer to 8-4 "App Fusion")
The explanation for app fusion is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
Assembly Requirements
The requirements for Assembly. (For details, refer to 7-3 "Assembly")
The explanation for Assembly requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
Lower Text
This refers to the text below the traits on a card. "INHERITED EFFECT", "SECURITY", "LINK", or "OPTION" will be shown for this text. Some cards don't have lower text.
Inherited Effects
An inherited effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the text marked "Inherited Effect" on a card. (For details, refer to 15-3 "Inherited Effects")

When a rule or effect references the "Inherited Effect" part of card information, the text marked "Inherited Effect" on a card is to be referenced. A card without an inherited effect section can't be referenced.
SECURITY
This is a [Security] effect. Some [Security] effects aren't shown in the lower text. (For details, refer to 15-16-10 "[Security]")
Link
This information indicates that a card has [Link]. The link requirements, link DP, and link effects will be shown for a link. (For details, refer to 10 "Linking")
The link requirements show the information and the required link cost for 1 Digimon that can link with that card.
The link cost is the cost required to link that card.
The explanation for link requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
The link DP shows the DP value added to the DP of the Digimon linked to that card.
A link effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the text shown for the link effect on a card.
When a rule or effect references the "link effect" part of card information, the text for a link effect on a card is to be referenced. If a card doesn't have a link effect, it can't be referenced.
Option Information
"Option information" refers to the lower text on a DUAL card.
Color
This information indicates the color of a card.
Colors include red, blue, yellow, green, black, purple, and white. When choosing a color by a rule or an effect, one of these colors is to be chosen.
If a single card has multiple colors, that card is a "multicolor" card.
A multicolor card is also treated as having all of its colors.
A multicolor card can't be treated as a card that doesn't have one of those colors.
DP (Digimon Power)
This information indicates a card's strength in battles. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")

When a rule or effect references a card's original DP, this value is to be referenced. However, if the DP was modified by an effect, the modified DP will be referenced. (For details, refer to 15-12-2 "Effects That Modify Information")
DP can't be added if a card doesn't have DP. (Example: +3000 DP can't be added if a Digimon doesn't have DP, nor can its DP be reduced by-3000.
Play Cost
A card's play cost refers to the cost required to play that card. This is shown using a "Play" icon.
Use Cost
A use cost refers to the cost required to use that card. This is shown using a "Use" icon.
Digi-Egg Icon
This information indicates that a card is a Digi-Egg card.
Lv. (Level)
This information indicates the card's level.
Cards that have no level displayed, or with "Lv. －" shown, are treated as having no level.
Overflow
This information indicates that a card has Overflow. (For details, refer to 4-17 "<Overflow>")
The explanation for Overflow requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6"Notes")
Arts Digivolve
This information indicates that a card has Arts Digivolve. (For details, refer to 4-19 "Arts Digivolve")
The explanation for Arts Digivolve is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-13-1-6 "Notes")
Card Number
This is a card's sequential number. If cards have matching card names and card numbers, they're considered to be the same card.
Other Information
Other information on a card can't be referenced during a game.
Illustration
The illustration for the card.
Illustrator Name
The name of the illustrator for the card.
Copyright Notice
The copyright notice for the card.
Rarity
How rare a card is.
Block Icon
This icon indicates the time period when this card was released.
Notes
These are explanations in text.
Notes for effects are shown in parentheses.
Sometimes a rule or effect will have notes and sometimes it won't, but they are treated the same in both situations.
Game Areas
Areas
Areas include the deck, Digi-Egg deck, field, hand, trash, and security stack.
Public Areas and Private Areas
Public Areas
All card information on cards in these areas is revealed to both players. Either player may look at the content or card order of these areas at any time.
Private Areas
Card information on cards in these areas isn't revealed to both players. Neither player may look at the content or card order of these areas.
Area Rules
New Cards
When a card is moved from one area to another, that card becomes a "new card."
A new card is considered to be a different card from the card in the previous area, and it will not carry over any of the original card's statuses, states, etc.
Even if a card on the field becomes the bottom card in a stack due to cards being placed on top of it, it isn't considered to be a new card.
Even if the stacking order of stacked cards changes, they aren't considered new cards.
The number of cards in each area is public information.
When multiple cards leave an area at the same time and are then placed in a different area, they are all considered to leave and be placed at the same time rather than 1 card at a time.

When multiple cards leave an area at the same time, the player who owns the card that caused the action to be performed chooses the order in which the cards are placed in the new area. (Example: When "[When Digivolving] Return all of your opponent's Digimon with the highest level to the bottom of the deck in any order" is used to return multiple opponent's Digimon to the bottom of the deck at the same time, the player who activated this effect chooses the order in which the cards are placed at the bottom of the deck.)

When placing a card in an area, unless otherwise specified, it's placed according to the rules of that area. (Example: When "[On Deletion] Place this card at the bottom of your security stack" is used to place a card at the bottom of the security stack, it's placed face down.)
When multiple cards are moved from a public area then placed into a private area at the same time, they are placed after the order is made public.
If a card's information contains instructions, when placing that card in a private area, the card is placed after revealing it.
When card text specifies that a card is to be placed in an area without specifying which player's area, the card is placed in the area of the player who owns the card.
When Digi-Egg cards are placed from respective areas to private areas, they are placed according to the following rules.
If placing in the deck or Digi-Egg deck, cards are placed in the Digi-Egg deck in the specified order.
If placing in private areas other than the deck or Digi-Egg deck, cards are placed at the bottom of the Digi-Egg deck.
Deck
This is the area where you place your deck at the start of the game.
The deck is a private area. Cards are placed face-down in this area.
Players can't change the order of cards in their decks.
When multiple cards are moved from the deck to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.
Digi-Egg Deck
This is the area where you place your Digi-Egg deck at the start of the game.
The Digi-egg deck is a private area. Cards are placed face-down in this area.
Players can't change the order of cards in their Digi-Egg decks.
When multiple cards are moved from the Digi-Egg deck to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.
Field
This is the main area of the game where cards are placed.
The field is a public area. Cards are placed face-up in this area.
When cards are placed in the field, they are placed unsuspended. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")
Each card placed on the field is treated as a separate Digimon or Tamer, etc.

If another card is stacked on top of a card on the field, or if the card stacked on top leaves and the card underneath is a different card, it will be considered to have changed to that Digimon or Tamer, etc. It won't be considered a different Digimon or Tamer, etc. (Example: If a player's [GrapLeomon] digivolves into [Marsmon], that [GrapLeomon] will be considered to change into [Marsmon], it won't be treated as a [Marsmon] that is newly placed onto the field.)
The field is divided into the breeding area and the battle area.
Breeding Area
This is the part of the field where hatched Digimon are placed.
Only 1 card can be placed in the breeding area.
Cards in breeding areas can't be affected by effects, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (For details, refer to 15-15-6 "Isn't affected by effects" cards")

Effects on cards in breeding areas can't trigger or activate, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even when a Digimon with a [When Digivolving] effect in a breeding area digivolves, its [When Digivolving] effect doesn't trigger.)

Cards in breeding areas can't be chosen for effects, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: A Digimon in your opponent's breeding area can't be chosen for "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon."

Trigger conditions can't be met by cards in breeding areas, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if your Digimon in the breeding area digivolves during your turn, a "[Your Turn] When your Digimon digivolves, by suspending this Tamer, <Draw 1>" effect doesn't trigger.)

Activation conditions can't be met by cards in breeding areas, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if your opponent has a Digimon in the breeding area at the start of your main phase, a "[Start of Your Main Phase] If your opponent has a Digimon, gain 1 memory" effect doesn't trigger.)

Information on cards in breeding areas can't be referenced, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if you have a Digimon with the [Armor Form] trait in the breeding area, you can't ignore the color requirements when a "while you have a Digimon with the [Armor Form] trait, you may ignore this card's color requirements" effect activates.
Battle Area
This is the part of the field where cards are placed.
Any number of cards can be placed in the battle area.
Hand
This is the area where cards held by each player are placed.
Players can change the order of cards in their respective hand at any time.
The hand is a private area, but the cards' owner may always look at their hand.
Trash
The trash is the area where trashed cards are placed.
Players can change the order of cards in their respective trash at any time.
The trash is a public area. Cards are placed face-up in a stack in this area.
The Security Stack
Security cards are placed in this area.
The security stack is a private area. Cards in this area are placed face-down and spread out so that the number of cards can be seen.
Players can't change the order of cards in their security stacks.
If a face-up card is placed in a security stack, the card becomes public information.
When multiple cards are moved from the security stack to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.
Basic Game Terminology
Memory
Memory refers to the resource used to pay for in-game costs.

"X or less memory" refers to X on your side of the memory gauge or further to the right. "X or more memory" refers to X on your side of the memory gauge or further to the left. (Example: "[Start of Your Turn] If you have 2 or less memory, set it to 3" includes a condition where the memory must be at 2 on your side or further to the right.)

"If your opponent has X or less memory" refers to X on your opponent's side of the memory gauge or further to the left. "If your opponent has X or more memory" refers to X on your opponent's side of the memory gauge or further to the right. (Example: A "[When Digivolving] <Blitz> (This Digimon can attack when your opponent has 1 or more memory)" effect includes a condition where the memory must be at 1 on your opponent's side or further to the right.)

"Gain X memory" means moving the memory marker X spaces toward your side (the left side) of the memory gauge. "Lose X memory" means moving the memory marker X spaces toward your opponent's side (the right side) of the memory gauge.
Costs
A cost is a numerical value that is required to be paid using memory. A card's cost and "pay X cost" are both examples of costs.

To pay a cost, the player moves the memory gauge toward the opponent's side (to their right) by an amount equal to the numerical value of the cost. When paying, the value indicated is paid, and no more and no less than that value can be paid.
Alternate Costs

If a cost's numerical value increases or decreases, that becomes an alternate cost. When a cost becomes an alternate cost, no more and no less than that value can be paid. (Example: If a card with a play cost of 12 activates the effect "When this card would be played, if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer, reduce the cost by 5," the cost to be paid becomes an alternate cost of 7.)
Digimon
Digi-Egg cards and Digimon cards placed on the field are treated as Digimon.
Cards stacked under Digimon are considered "digivolution cards," regardless of their card category. (For details, refer to 4-6 "Digivolution Cards")

A Digimon gains the inherited effects of the digivolution cards placed under it. (Example: If a Digimon has a digivolution card that has <Piercing> in its inherited effects, that Digimon will have <Piercing>.)
A Digimon gets the link DP value on its link card.
A Digimon gains the link effects on its link card.
Digimon in the battle area can attack. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")
Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area can block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
Digimon can perform 1 security check. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
Tamers
Tamer cards placed on the field are treated as Tamers.

When placing a card under a Tamer that already has cards stacked under it, unless specified otherwise, you place the new card at the bottom. (Example: If using <Save> to place a card under a Tamer that already has cards stacked under it, place the new card at the bottom.)
Security Digimon
A Digimon card flipped over from the security stack upon a security check is treated as a Security Digimon. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
DUAL Cards
A DUAL card is a card that can be treated as being in either the Digimon card category or the Option card category.
When utilizing a DUAL card, the player must declare whether they are digivolving with the Digimon information or using the Option information on that card.

A DUAL card placed on the field is treated as a Digimon. It can't be referenced as an Option card placed on the field. (Example: A DUAL card that is digivolved by placing it on top of one of your cards on the field will be treated as a Digimon, and it can't be trashed by a "trash an Option card in the battle area" effect.)
A single DUAL card has both Digimon information and Option information.
Digimon Information
This refers to a DUAL card's traits and the information above them.
A DUAL card's Digimon information can be referenced when referencing the card as a Digimon card or Digimon.
Effects in the Digimon information are considered Digimon effects. (For details, refer to 15-2 "Effect Types")
Option Information
This refers a DUAL card's traits and the information below them.
A DUAL card's Option information can be referenced when referencing the card as an Option card.
Effects in the Option information are treated as Option card effects. (For details, refer to 15-2 "Effect Types")
Stacked Cards
"Stacked cards" refers to all cards on the field that have 1 or more cards underneath them.
Only 1 card isn't considered "stacked cards."
The stacking order of cards can't be changed.

The bottom cards of a stack are spread out so that inherited effects are visible. A card without an inherited effect is placed in the stack so that its name is visible. A face-down card must be stacked so that it's clearly under the top card.
Unless specified otherwise, the bottom cards of a stack are placed face-up.

Bottom cards of a stack are placed vertically, but they don't have an orientation. When the bottom card of a stack becomes the top card, the stack's previous orientation is carried over. This isn't considered unsuspending or suspending of a card. (Example: When <De-Digivolve 1> is used to trash the top card of a suspended Digimon, the top card of the stack under it will carry over the suspended state.)

The bottom cards of a stack are treated as part of the information on the top card. They aren't considered to be placed on the field. (Example: When "[When Digivolving] Place one of your opponent's level 3 or lower Digimon under another of your opponent's Digimon as its bottom digivolution card or under an opponent's Tamer" is used to place a Digimon under a card, that card is considered to be removed from the field.)

When a card with cards stacked under it would be removed from the field, the cards under it are trashed at the same time. (Example: When a Digimon or Tamer would be removed from the battle area, any cards under it are trashed at the same time.)

A face-down card under another card is considered to be a card without card information, and its information can't be referenced. (Example: When a face-down digivolution card is placed for <Training>, information such as its card name or color can't be referenced for other effects.)
A face-down card under another card is hidden information, but the cards' owner may freely look at the content of a face-down card under one of their cards.
Digivolution Cards
A digivolution card refers to a card placed under a Digimon. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")
When referencing digivolution card information, the information is referenced on cards that are treated as digivolution cards.
Link cards
A link card is a card plugged in sideways upon a link.
A link card isn't considered a stacked card. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")

A link card is plugged in from the right and positioned so that the link portion of the card is visible. When multiple link cards are inserted under 1 card, a newly inserted link card must be placed so that its link portion is visible under the existing cards.
A link card isn't considered to be a card on the field. (For details, refer to 3-4 "The Field")

1 card can have a maximum of 1 link card. When linking to a Digimon that has already reached the link limit, the same number of the existing link cards are trashed at the same time as the newly linked cards.
If a card with a link card would become a new card, its link card is trashed at the same time. (For details, refer to 3-1-3-1 "New Cards")
Linked Cards
A linked card is a card that has a link card.
Players
A "player" refers to a game participant.
If a rule or effect specifies an "owner," it refers to the player that is currently using that card in the game.
"Opponent" refers to the other player in the game.
Turn Player and Non-Turn Player
The turn player refers to the player that is performing the procedures for the current turn, and the non-turn player refers to the other player.
Card Orientation
Cards on the field have an orientation. A card's orientation shows whether it is unsuspended or suspended.
Unsuspended
An "unsuspended" card refers to a card placed vertically.
"Unsuspended state" refers to an unsuspended card.
Suspended
A "suspended" card refers to a card placed horizontally.
"Suspended state" refers to a suspended card.
Draw
"Drawing" refers to drawing cards from the deck and placing them in the hand.
Unless specified otherwise by a rule or effect, a player draws cards from their own deck.
Deletion
When deletion processing is applied to a card by a rule or effect, that card is trashed.

An effect timing or keyword effect that triggers on deletion of the card itself does so in the area where the card is deleted , then becomes pending activation after that card is placed into the trash by destruction. (Example: An [On Deletion] effect triggers in the battle area, then becomes pending activation after the card is placed into the trash.)
Trashing Cards
"Trashing" refers to placing a card in the trash.

An effect that triggers on trashing of the card itself does so in the area where the card is trashed , then becomes pending activation after that card is placed into the trash by trashing. (Example: "When this card is trashed from your hand by one of your effects, <Draw 1>" will trigger while the card is in the hand, then it will become pending activation when the card is in the trash.)
Trashing isn't considered deletion.
Moving

"Moving" refers to moving a Digimon between the breeding area and the battle area. A player can move a Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area as one of their actions during the breeding phase.
Only Digimon with DP can be moved.
When a card is moved, it keeps its orientation. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")
Any effects applied to a Digimon before it moves are kept after the move.

If a Digimon is moved, the effects status of that Digimon isn't carried over. (Example: If a Digimon has an effect that's pending activation when it's moved, that effect will no longer be pending activation.) (For details, refer to 15-4 "Effect States") 15-4
Hatching a Digi-Egg

"Hatching" refers to flipping over the top card of your Digi-Egg deck and placing it in the specified area. You can hatch a Digi-Egg from the top of your Digi-Egg deck into the breeding area as one of your actions during the breeding phase.
You can't hatch a Digi-Egg if you don't have any cards in your Digi-Egg deck.
You can't hatch a Digi-Egg if you already have a card in the breeding area.
Overflow

<Overflow> is a rule on Digimon ACE cards. When a card with <Overflow> moves from the field or from under a card to another area, the memory marker is moved according to the value specified for <Overflow>.
When <Overflow> causes the memory marker to move, the processing for moving it is performed immediately, even if the processing for another action is already being performed.
<Overflow> isn't processed when a card is moved from another area to the field. (For details, refer to 3-4 "The Field")
<Overflow> isn't processed when a card is moved from another area to under a card. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")
When multiple instances of <Overflow> are processed simultaneously, they are processed using the following procedure.
The turn player chooses 1 instance of <Overflow> on their cards and processes it. The turn player repeats this procedure until there are no more unresolved instances of <Overflow> on their cards.

Once all instances of <Overflow> on the turn player's cards have been processed, then the non-turn player chooses 1 instance of <Overflow> on their cards and processes it. The non-turn player repeats this procedure until there are no more unresolved instances of <Overflow> on their cards.
Arts Digivolve

Arts Digivolve is a rule on DUAL cards. Instead of the trashing from the pending processing after using an Option card, one of your cards on the field may digivolve into that DUAL card without paying the cost.
Arts Digivolve is overwrite processing that replaces the trashing of an Option card from the pending processing. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")
Tokens
Tokens are non-game cards played by effects. Such effects play tokens as if they have card information.
The number of tokens is always public information.
Cards can't be stacked with tokens.
Tokens can't get linked.
When a token leaves the field, it is removed from the game instead of being placed in another area. However, the token itself is considered to be placed in that area.
Color Requirements
"Color requirements" refers to a requirement that must be met in order to use an Option card. (For details, refer to 9 "Using Cards")
To meet color requirements, you must have a Digimon or Tamer on your field that's the same color as the Option card you want to use.
An Option card with multiple colors can't be used unless the color requirements are met for all of its colors.
A multicolor Digimon or multicolor Tamer can meet the color requirements for multiple colors.
An Option card's color requirements don't have to be met when activating its effects without using it.
Cards "With XX in Their Texts"

A "with XX in its text" card is a card that has the "XX" term or icon in the information printed on that card. (Example: A "card with <Save> in its text" refers to a card with the <Save> icon included in the information on that card.) (For details, refer to 2-3 "Information Written on Cards")

When an effect is gained, that doesn't mean that text is gained. (Example: A Digimon won't gain the <Save> text from a digivolution card whose inherited effect reads "[Your Turn] While this Digimon has <Save> in its text, it gets +2000 DP.")

When a card with an effect's text is specified, as long as the card has that text written on it, it can be referenced even in situations where the effect can't be triggered or activated. (Example: A card with <Save> shown in its inherited effect is considered a card with <Save> in its text even when that card isn't placed in digivolution cards.)

When a card with an icon's text is specified, only a card with the matching icon can be referenced. (Example: When an effect specifies a card with <Save> in its text, <Material Save> can't be referenced because its icon isn't the same.)
Notes aren't included in text. (Example: A Digimon card with <Alliance> and <Security A.> in the notes enclosed in parentheses for Alliance isn't considered to have <Security A.> in its text.)
"XX/YY"

When a card shows "XX/YY," it means the same as "XX or YY," and either one of them will meet a requirement. However, this doesn't include when individual traits are separated by slashes. (Example: "[On Play] 1 of your opponent's Digimon/Tamers can't suspend until the end of their turn" means that you choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon or Tamers, then the chosen card can't suspend.)
"With different XX" Cards
A "with different XX" card refers to a card whose information is different from the information specified using XX.
If a card that has multiple instances of the information specified by XX, the differing portions can be referenced and be treated as differing combinations.
"With/have X cards"

"With/have X cards" refers to a requirement that is fulfilled when that number of cards is present. (Example: "[On Play] When this Digimon has 3 digivolution cards, <Blitz>" can be activated if that Digimon has 3 or more digivolution cards.)
"Each" or "Every"
"Each" or "every" is used when an effect references a number of something.

Processing that targets "for each X" number of stacked cards from the top or bottom targets up to that number of cards in order starting from that position in the stack. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Digivolving] For each of your Digimon with the [Royal Knight] trait or each of your blue Tamers, trash the top 2 digivolution cards of 1 of your opponent's Digimon" and you have 2 blue Tamers, you would choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon and trash its top 4 digivolution cards.)

In the case of a "process A and process B" effect that applies to each X, after processing A for each X present upon activation, you then process B for each X present upon activation. (Example: For text that reads "[End of Opponent’s Turn] [Once Per Turn] For each of this Digimon's link cards, trash your opponent's top security card and return 1 of their Digimon to the bottom of the deck," if that Digimon is linked to 3 cards, you trash your opponent's top 3 security cards and then return 3 of their Digimon to the bottom of the deck.

A triggering from 1 trigger condition is considered to only trigger once, even if it occurred multiple times at the same time, but if the effect text contains "each" or "every," the specified number can be referenced. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] When an opponent's Digimon is deleted, gain 1 memory for each Digimon deleted" and multiple opponent Digimon are deleted at the same time, 1 memory is gained for each Digimon deleted.)
"Option Card in the Battle Area"

An "Option card in the battle area" refers to an Option card that was placed in the battle area by an effect. (Example: A "trash an Option card in the battle area" effect can only trash an Option card that was placed in the battle area by an effect.)
"Also"

"Also" indicates that effects given by that processing share the same duration and targets as the processing that proceeded them. (Example: "They also" in the effect "{Security} [Your Turn] All of your red or blue [TS] trait Digimon gain <Alliance>. While you have [Apollomon] or [Dianamon], they also gain <Rush>" refers to your red or blue [TS] trait Digimon.)
Game Preparation
Deck and Digi-Egg Deck Preparation
Before beginning a game, both players prepare the items required for a game. (For details, refer to 1-4 "Items Required for a Game")
Token cards are left outside of the game at this point.

Place the Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules) to the side of your play sheet or away from your other cards. (For details, refer to 1-4-5 "Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules)")
Pre-Game Preparations
Before the game begins, both players must perform the following steps.
Each player shuffles their respective deck. Then, both players place their deck face down.
Each player shuffles their respective Digi-Egg deck. Then, both players place their Digi-Egg deck face down. If you don't have a Digi-Egg deck, proceed directly to the next step.
The players use rock-paper-scissors to determine the first player and the second player. The player who wins the game of rock-paper-scissors goes first.

Both players draw 5 cards from their decks for their initial hands. Then, both players starting with the first player may declare to re-draw their initial hand, but this can only be done once by each player.
After declaring a re-draw, the player returns their entire hand to their deck, shuffles it, then draws 5 cards for their new initial hand.

For their security stack, both players take the top 5 cards of their deck and place them face-down one at a time without looking at the fronts of the cards. The cards are to be placed so the top card of the deck becomes the bottom card of the security stack.
Place the memory gauge marker at the 0 position.
The game begins with the first player's turn.
Game Procedures
Turn Procedures
A game will proceed with one of the players as the turn player.
A turn proceeds using phases in the following order. Unsuspend phase, draw phase, breeding phase, and main phase.
The next phase won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current phase.
Turn End Conditions

The turn end conditions are met when the memory is at 1 or more on your opponent's side and all processing has been resolved for the current phase. Then, the turn will end with the current phase. (For details, refer to 6-6 "End of Turn")
Unsuspend Phase
The turn starts with the turn player unsuspending all of their cards on the field at the same time.

If there are any rules or effects to be processed when the turn starts, the processing takes place before the unsuspending processing for the unsuspend phase. (Example: "[Start of Your Turn] If you have 2 or less memory, set it to 3" is processed before the unsuspending processing for the unsuspend phase.)
If processing for any rules or effects has been resolved when the turn starts and the turn end conditions have been met, the end of the turn timing occurs before unsuspending.
Cards don't have to be unsuspended in any particular order for the unsuspend phase.
Draw Phase
The turn player draws 1 card.
The first player doesn't draw a card during the draw phase of their first turn. A card must be drawn in all subsequent draw phases.
Breeding Phase
1 of the following actions can be performed by the turn player during the breeding phase. Hatch a Digi-Egg, move a card from the breeding area to the battle area, or do nothing.
"Hatch a Digi-Egg" means taking the top card of your Digi-Egg deck and placing it face-up in the breeding area. (For details, refer to 4-16 "Hatching a Digi-Egg")
"Move a card from the breeding area to the battle area" means moving your Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area. (For details, refer to 4-15 "Moving Cards")
"Do nothing" means proceeding to the next phase without doing anything.
Main Phase

During the main phase, the turn player can perform the following actions in any order any number of times. These actions are to be performed when there is no unresolved processing. Play a Digimon card or Tamer card from the hand, digivolve into a Digimon card from the hand, use an Option card from the hand, link a card from the hand or battle area, attack, activate an activation-type effect, or pass.
Play a Digmon Card or Tamer Card From the Hand
This action is where the cost is paid for a Digimon card or Tamer card in the hand in order to play it into the battle area. (For details, refer to 7-1 "Playing a Card")
When performing this action, it is also possible to DigiXros the played Digimon card. (For details, refer to 7-2 "DigiXros")
When performing this action, it is also possible to use [Assembly] on the played Digimon card. (For details, refer to 7-3 "Assembly")
Digivolve Into a Digimon Card From the Hand
Digivolving a Digimon is an action where a player's card on the field is digivolved into 1 Digimon card in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-1 "Digivolving")

This action can also be used to digivolve multiple Digimon in your battle area into 1 Digimon card with [DNA Digivolution] in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")
This action can also be used to digivolve one of your cards on the field into 1 Digimon card with [Burst Digivolve] by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-3 "Burst Digivolve")
This action can also be used to digivolve 1 of a player's Digimon in the battle area into 1 Digimon card with [App Fusion] in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-4 "App Fusion")
Use an Option Card From the Hand
This action is where a player pays the cost for an Option card in the hand to use it from their hand. (For details, refer to 9-1 "Using Cards")
Linking a Card in the Hand or Battle Area
This action is where 1 card from the hand or battle area is linked with 1 of your Digimon in the battle area. (For details, refer to 10 "Linking")
Attacking
This action is where a player uses their Digimon in the battle area to attack. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")
Activating Activation-Type Effects
This action is where a player activates 1 activation-type effect on one of their cards.
Passing
This action is where a player declares a pass. After declaring a pass, the memory is immediately moved to 3 on the opponent's side.
End of Turn
When the turn end conditions are met, the end of the turn timing occurs in that phase. (For details, refer to 6-1-4 "Turn End Conditions")
Even if the timing for the end of the turn arrives, the current phase will continue until all processing has been resolved.
Once all processing has been resolved for the end of the turn timing, the turn ends, then the non-turn player's turn will begin.
If the memory moves to 0 or more during the end of the turn timing, ending the turn will be postponed and the current phase will continue.
Playing a Card
Playing a Card

"Playing a card" refers to a rule where a player can place a new card with a play cost onto the field. A card can be played from a player's hand into the battle area as part of their main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")
Card Playing Rules
A Digimon or Tamer, etc. can't attack on the turn it was placed on the field.
Immediate-type effects that trigger when a card would be played will trigger immediately after the card is revealed during the play procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

If a card can no longer be played after revealing it as part of the procedure for playing it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be played because its cost can't be paid.
The processing for playing a card is performed using the following procedure.
The player declares to play a card and reveals that card.
The player pays the specified play cost. (For details, refer to 2-6 "Play Costs")
The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.
DigiXros

A DigiXros refers to a rule where a player plays a Digimon card with DigiXros requirements, places any number of the cards specified in that card's DigiXros requirements from their hand and/or battle area under the Digimon card to be played, and the play cost is reduced by the value specified in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed. This is shown on cards using text such as "DigiXros-2: [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]×[Dorulumon]×[Starmon s]."
DigiXros Rules

When performing a DigiXros, the play cost is reduced by the amount shown in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed for the DigiXros. (Example: For DigiXros requirements that read "DigiXros-1: [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]," a player can place [Shoutmon] and/or [Ballistamon] cards under the played card, and the play cost of the played card is reduced by 1 for each card placed.)

A declaration for a DigiXros is made immediately before paying the play cost. If any effects are triggered when the card would be played, the DigiXros declaration comes after such effects. (Example: In order to perform a DigiXros using a card with both DigiXros requirements and a "when this card would be played" effect, first the effect is resolved, then you declare the DigiXros.)

You declare the DigiXros at the same time as when you choose the cards to place under the card to be played for the DigiXros. After you have chosen all of the cards to place under the card to be played, place them under that card. Once placed, additional cards to place can't be chosen. (Example: Even if you activate a "when this Digimon would leave the battle area, return 1 yellow Digimon card from this Digimon's digivolution cards to the hand" effect when placing the cards chosen for a DigiXros under the c ard to be played, the cards returned to the hand by this effect can't be placed under the card to be played for this DigiXros.)
A player can place any number of the cards specified in the DigiXros requirements for a DigiXros. However, if a DigiXros has been declared, the player can't choose to place 0 cards.
1 of each of the cards specified in the DigiXros requirements can be placed for the DigiXros. However, if a DigiXros has the number of cards specified, only up to that number of cards can be placed.
When cards will be placed under a card from the hand for a DigiXros, that card is to be revealed from the hand at the same time as the declaration for the DigiXros.
If a DigiXros is used to place a card in the battle area under a card, the placed card is considered to leave the field at that timing.

When cards placed for a DigiXros are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the Digimon shown on the left side of the DigiXros requirements goes on top. If the DigiXros requirements specify the numbers of each card, the player performing the DigiXros chooses the stacking order.

A DigiXros is considered to be performed when 1 or more cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros. If 0 cards are placed under the card to be played, a DigiXros isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares a DigiXros. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Attacking] You may give 1 of your opponent's Digimon <Security A. -1> until the end of their turn. Then, if DigiXrosing, this Digimon gets +3000 DP and <Blocker> until the end of your opponent's turn," it will be possible to perform the "if DigiXrosing" and later part of the effect only if a card is placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros.)

An X-card DigiXros is considered to be performed when X cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros. If X cards aren't placed under the card to be played, an X-card DigiXros isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares a DigiXros. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] <De-Digivolve 1> 1 of your opponent's Digimon, then if DigiXrosing with 2 cards, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a play cost of 5 or less," it will be possible to perform the "if DigiXrosing with 2 cards" and later part of the effect only if 2 cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros.)
If a card can no longer be played while a DigiXros procedure is being performed, the cards placed under it are trashed.
A DigiXros isn't mandatory.
Effects that affect playing cards will also affect playing cards for a DigiXros.
The processing for a DigiXros is performed using the following procedure.
During the play procedure, the player proceeds up to the step where the card to play is revealed, then if any effects trigger upon play, those effects are to be resolved.

A DigiXros is declared immediately before paying the play cost. At the same time, the desired cards to be placed under the card to be played as specified in the DigiXros requirements are chosen from the cards in the hand and/or battle area.

The chosen cards are placed under the card to be played. The play cost is reduced by the amount shown in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed for the DigiXros. When paying a play cost, the player pays the cost after any increases or reductions.
The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.
Assembly

Assembly refers to a rule where a player plays a Digimon card with Assembly requirements, places the specified number of the cards specified in that card's Assembly requirements from their trash under the Digimon card to be played, and the play cost is reduced by the value specified in that card's Assembly requirements. This is shown on cards using text such as "Assembly-6: 4 [Negamon] cards."
Assembly Rules

By placing the cards specified in the Assembly requirements under the card to be played, Assembly will reduce the play cost as specified in the Assembly requirements. (Example: For Assembly requirements that read "Assembly-6: 4 [Negamon] cards," a player can use Assembly to place 4 [Negamon] cards under the card to be played, and the play cost will be reduced by 6.)
A declaration for Assembly is made immediately before paying the play cost. If any effects are triggered when the card would be played, the Assembly declaration comes after such effects.

You declare Assembly at the same time as when you choose the cards to place under the card to be played for Assembly. After the player has chosen all of the cards to place under the card to be played, they place them under that card. Once placed, additional cards to place can't be chosen.
The exact number of cards specified in the Assembly requirements must be placed for the Assembly. A player can't place just some of the specified cards.

1 of each of the cards shown in the Assembly requirements can be placed under the card to be played for Assembly. However, if Assembly specifies the number of cards, only that number of cards can be placed.

When cards placed for Assembly are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the card shown on the left side of the Assembly requirements goes on top. If the Assembly requirements specify the same cards or the numbers of each card, the player performing the Assembly chooses the stacking order.
If no cards are placed under the card to be played, an Assembly isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares an Assembly.
If a card can no longer be played while the Assembly procedure is being performed, the cards placed under it are trashed.
Assembly isn't mandatory.
Assembly can be performed even when an effect is used to play a Digimon card with Assembly requirements.
The processing for Assembly is performed using the following procedure.
During the play procedure, the player proceeds up to the step where the card to play is revealed, then if any effects trigger upon play, those effects are to be resolved.

Declare an Assembly immediately before paying the play cost. At the same time, the cards to be placed under the card to be played as specified in the Assembly requirements are chosen from the cards in the trash.

The chosen cards are placed under the card to be played. The play cost is reduced by the amount specified in the Assembly requirements. When paying a play cost, the player pays the cost after any increases or reductions.
The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.
Digivolution
Digivolution

Digivolution refers to a rule that allows a player to reveal a Digimon card and stack it on top of their card on the field to change that card. A player can digivolve a card on the field into their Digimon card by paying its cost as part of their main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")
Digivolution Rules
When 1 card has multiple digivolution requirements, the player chooses the digivolution requirement for the revealed card. For details, refer to 2-3-6 "Digivolution Requirements")

If ignoring the digivolution requirements when digivolving, the digivolution will occur regardless of the digivolution requirements. Even if a card has digivolution requirements, they aren't referenced. If it doesn't have digivolution requirements, digivolution is still possible.
A digivolved Digimon carries over its orientation from before the digivolution. (Example: When digivolving a suspended Digimon, the Digimon card stacked on top will also be suspended.)

Immediate-type effects that trigger when digivolution would occur will trigger immediately after the card is revealed and the card for digivolution is chosen during the digivolution procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
1 digivolution can only be performed on 1 Digimon. You can't perform separate digivolutions on multiple cards at the same time.

If a card can no longer be digivolved after revealing it as part of the procedure for digivolving it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be digivolved because its cost can't be paid.
Digivolution isn't considered adding to a Digimon's digivolution cards.
Digivolution is also possible in situations where a draw isn't possible. In such cases, the digivolution processing is performed without drawing a card.
The processing for digivolution is performed using the following procedure.

The player declares a digivolution and reveals 1 Digimon card for the digivolution. 1 digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses 1 of their cards on the field that meets the requirement.
The digivolution cost specified in the chosen digivolution requirement is paid. (For details, refer to 2-3-6 "Digivolution Requirements")
The player places the Digimon for the digivolution on top of the chosen card, draws 1 card, and the digivolution process is resolved.
DNA Digivolution

DNA digivolution is a rule where 1 Digimon card with [DNA Digivolution] is revealed and multiples of a player's cards that meet the revealed card's DNA digivolution requirements are stacked in the order as shown in the requirements, changing the stacked cards and revealed card by digivolving it into 1 new Digimon. This is shown on cards using text such as "[DNA Digivolution] Blue Lv.4 + green Lv.4: Cost 0"
DNA Digivolution Rules

DNA digivolution differs from standard digivolution in that the cards that become digivolution cards digivolve as different Digimon or Tamers, etc. A DNA digivolved Digimon doesn't carry over the states of the cards that become digivolution cards. Instead, they are treated as follows.
The card placed on top digivolves unsuspended without carrying over the Digimon's orientation from before the digivolution. That Digimon isn't considered to switch from suspended to unsuspended.

All cards that become digivolution cards are considered to be new cards. If a Digimon has a link card from before the digivolution, the link card is trashed immediately before placing the Digimon as a digivolution card.
If a Digimon was attacking before a digivolution, the attacking Digimon is considered to be no longer present. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")
If a Digimon was an attack target before a digivolution, the attack target is considered to be no longer present. (For details, refer to 11-2-7 "Attack Targets")
If a Digimon was chosen for an effect or if any effects were applied to it before a digivolution, all those effects end. (For details, refer to 15-13 "Gained Effects")
Any [X Per Turn] uses on a DNA digivolved card will be reset. (For details, refer to 15-14-1 "X Per Turn")
If a Digimon digivolves during the same turn it was played, it loses the information stating that it was played that turn, and it can now attack during that turn.

When cards placed for DNA digivolution are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the Digimon shown on the left side of [DNA Digivolution] goes on top. If the numbers of each card or multiples of a card are specified in [DNA Digivolution], the player performing the DNA digivolution chooses the stacking order.

The Digimon that will become digivolution cards for a DNA digivolution are placed along with their own digivolution cards in the digivolution cards of the DNA digivolved Digimon. At such times, the stacking order of the digivolution cards can't be changed.
DNA digivolution can only be performed by an effect that specifically performs DNA digivolution. DNA digivolution can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

Effects that affect digivolution will also affect DNA digivolution. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would DNA digivolve.)
The processing for DNA digivolution is performed using the following procedure.

The player declares a DNA digivolution and reveals 1 Digimon card for the DNA digivolution. 1 DNA digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses their multiple cards that meet the requirement.
The digivolution cost specified in the chosen DNA digivolution requirement is paid.

The cards chosen to become digivolution cards are placed along with their own digivolution cards. The player places the Digimon for the DNA digivolution on top of the stack, draws 1 card, and the DNA digivolution process is resolved.
Burst Digivolve

Burst digivolve is a rule where a player reveals 1 Digimon card with [Burst Digivolve] and returns 1 of their Tamers from the battle area as specified in the [Burst Digivolve] card's burst digivolve requirements in order to digivolve one of their cards specified in the revealed card's burst digivolve requirements into the revealed card. This is shown on cards using text such as "Burst Digivolve [ShineGreymon]: By returning 1 [Marcus Damon] to the hand, cost 0."
Burst Digivolve Rules

When digivolution is performed by burst digivolve, as part of the pending processing, the top card of the digivolved Digimon's stack is trashed at the end of the turn it digivolved. However, if there are no stacked cards or that card is not a Digimon, no card is trashed. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")
Burst digivolve can only be performed by an effect that specifically performs burst digivolve. Burst digivolve can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

Effects that affect digivolution will also affect Burst Digivolve. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would burst digivolve.)
The processing for burst digivolve is performed using the following procedure.

The player declares a burst digivolve and reveals 1 Digimon card for the burst digivolve. 1 burst digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses one of their cards on the field that meets the requirement.
The player's Tamer specified in [Burst Digivolve] is returned from the battle area to the hand.
The digivolution cost specified in the chosen burst digivolve requirement is paid.
The player places the Digimon for the burst digivolve on top of the chosen card, draws 1 card, and the burst digivolve process is resolved.
App Fusion

App fusion is a rule where a player reveals 1 Digimon card with [App Fusion], chooses a pair of linked cards in the battle area from 2 of the specified cards in the revealed card's app fusion digivolution requirements, and stacks the link card of the chosen cards on top of that Digimon, digivolving the stacked cards into the revealed card. This is shown on cards using text such as "[App Fusion] [Gatchmon] & [Navimon] & [Tweetmon]: Cost 0."
App Fusion Rules

App fusion allows a linked Digimon to digivolve using a combination of 2 different specified cards. (Example: If "[App Fusion] [Gatchmon] & [Navimon] & [Tweetmon]: Cost 0" is specified, a linked Digimon consisting of a combination of 2 cards from among [Gatchmon], [Navimon], and [Tweetmon] can app fuse.)
App fusion by an effect can only be performed by effects that specifically perform app fusion. App fusion can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

Effects that affect digivolution will also affect app fusion. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would app fuse.)
The processing for app fusion is performed using the following procedure.

The player declares app fusion and reveals 1 Digimon card to app fuse. 1 app fusion digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses one of their cards in the battle area that meets the requirement.
The digivolution cost specified in the chosen app fusion digivolution requirement is paid.

A link card on the chosen card is placed on top of that Digimon as specified in the app fusion digivolution requirements. The player places it on top of the Digimon card to app fuse, draws 1 card, and the app fusion process is resolved.
Using Cards
Using Cards
Using a card refers to a rule where an Option card's [Main] effect is activated. When using a card, its color requirements must be met. For details, refer to 4-19 "Color Requirements")
If an Option card is used, its [Main] effect will activate. Other effects and rule checks don't interrupt the period between use and activation.

When using an Option card, if its [Main] effect has conditions, the effect can be activated when the conditions are met. (Example: If an effect reads "[Main] By trashing 1 card in your hand, delete 1 of your opponent's level 6 or lower Digimon. If this effect trashed a card with the [Seven Great Demon Lords] trait, place this card in the battle area," and you trash a card from your hand after using that Option card, you delete 1 of your opponent's level 6 or lower Digimon.)
A used Option card is treated as not being in any area during the period from activation of its 1st [Main] effect until it's been resolved.

A used Option card is immediately trashed as pending processing as soon as the timing when its 1st [Main] effect has been resolved, unless that Option card is considered to be placed in an area. Other effects and rule checks don't interrupt the period between [Main] effect activation and trashing. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")
Immediate-type effects that trigger when a card would be used will trigger immediately after the card is revealed during the use procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
Cards are used 1 at a time. Multiple cards can't be used at the same time.

If a card can no longer be used after revealing it as part of the procedure for using it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be used because its cost can't be paid.
