The processing for using an Option card is performed using the following procedure.
The player declares use of a card and reveals the Option card to be used.
The specified use cost is paid. (For details, refer to 2-7 "Use Costs")
When use of an Option card is resolved, its 1st [Main] effect is activated.
Link
Link

A link is a rule where a card with [Link] can link by plugging it in sideways into one of your specified Digimon on the field according to the link requirements. A card from the hand or battle area can be linked to a Digimon in the battle area by paying the cost as part of the main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")
Link Rules
If a card already has stacked cards, the new card is plugged in at the bottom. However, a linked card is not a stacked card.
A card plugged in sideways for a link becomes a link card. (For details, refer to 4-7 "Link Cards")

If an immediate-type effect triggers when linking would occur, it will trigger immediately after the card is revealed and the Digimon to be linked is chosen during the link procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
A link is performed using the following procedure.
The player declares a link and reveals 1 card to link. 1 link requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses 1 of their Digimon that meets the requirement.
The specified link cost is paid.
The card to link is plugged in sideways into the chosen Digimon, and the link procedure is resolved.
Attacking
Attack Procedure
This is a rule where a player can attack a chosen target Digimon in the battle area.
Only the turn player can attack.
An attack proceeds using the following timings: Attack declaration, counter timing, block timing, confirming if the attack is successful, and the end of the attack.

The next timing won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current timing. (Example: After declaring an attack, the counter timing won't begin until any triggered [When Attacking] effects and other triggered effects have been resolved.)

Once an attack declaration has been made, all of the timings that follow will occur. (Example: Even if an attacking Digimon leaves the battle area, the non-turn player's counter timing and block timing will still occur.)
Attack Declaration
The turn player can suspend their Digimon in the battle area and make an attack declaration.
At the same time as the attack declaration, the target of attack is chosen. (For details, refer to 11-2-7 "Attack Targets")
1 Digimon can perform 1 attack for an attack declaration. Multiple Digimon can't attack at the same time.
A new attack declaration can't be made during an attack. (Example: A new attack declaration can't be made using <Blitz> during an attack.)
An attack declaration can't be made using a Digimon that can't suspend.

Even if the attack target Digimon is removed during an attack, that Digimon remains the attack target, but the attack fails. (Example: Even if an attack target Digimon is deleted by a [When Attacking] effect, that Digimon remains the attack target. The attack fails because the attack target Digimon is removed.)
Attack Targets
When a player makes an attack declaration, they choose either the opponent or 1 of the opponent's suspended Digimon as the attack target.
After the attack declaration is made and an attack target is chosen, the attack target may switch to another target due to a rule or effect.
The attack target can't be switched to a target that is already an attack target.
If an attacking Digimon isn't in the battle area, its attack target can't be changed and its attack won't succeed on any target.

The processing for switching an attack target may affect the player that made the attack declaration. (Example: It is possible to switch the target of an attack by a Digimon that isn't affected by effects, and it is possible to switch the attack target to a Digimon that isn't affected by effects.)

If a trigger-type effect with text such as "if attacking XX" will be triggered by an attack, it will only trigger if the attack target chosen during the attack declaration procedure matches the target specified in the effect.
The processing for an attack declaration is performed using the following procedure.
The player makes an attack declaration, suspends 1 of their Digimon to make the attack in the battle area, and chooses an attack target.
Counter Timing
This is the timing when the [Counter] effect of a non-turn player who is being attacked can activate.
During the counter timing, only 1 [Counter] effect can be activated per attack.
Block Timing
This is the timing when a non-turn player who is being attacked can use their Digimon with <Blocker> to perform a block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
Confirming if an Attack is Successful

This is the timing when confirmation is performed to see if a Digimon's attack on the opponent player or an opponent's Digimon is successful. The following situations are confirmed during this timing.
The attacked player has 1 or more security cards, the Digimon's attack is on the opponent player, and the attack is successful
In this situation, the attacking Digimon will perform a security check on the attacked player. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
The attacked player has 0 security cards, the Digimon's attack is on the opponent player, and the attack is successful

In this situation, the player that made the attack declaration wins the game. However, they don't win if the attacking Digimon can't perform any security checks. For details, refer to 1-2-3 "Victory Conditions")
The Digimon's attack is on a Digimon, and the attack is successful
In this situation, a battle occurs between the attacking Digimon and the attacked Digimon. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")
The Digimon's attack is not successful
In this situation, no other actions are taken and the end of attack timing occurs.
End of Attack
The end of attack timing arrives and the attack ends.
For the end of the attack timing, the attack won't end until all processing has been resolved.
Blocking
Blocking
A block is a rule that allows a player to switch an attack target to a Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area. (For details, refer to 16-4 "<Blocker>")
A block can only be performed once per attack. Multiple Digimon can't block at the same time.
A new block declaration can't be made during a block.
A block can't be performed using a Digimon that can't suspend.
The attack target Digimon can't perform a block.
A block can only be performed if an attacking Digimon is in the battle area.
The processing for a block is performed using the following procedure.
The player makes a block declaration and suspends 1 of their Digimon in the battle area that will perform the block.
Security Checks
Security Checks
A security check is a rule that allows a player to perform a check on the opponent's security stack.

Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack. However, if the number of cards that can be checked is modified by an effect on the attacking Digimon, the modified number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
A security check is performed one card at a time.
If a security check is to be performed, it is mandatory.
If the Digimon performing the security check is no longer present in the battle area, that card can't perform any more security checks.
A checked card is removed from the security stack and is treated as not being in any particular area.
A checked Digimon card is treated as a Security Digimon.
A security check is performed using the following procedure.
Security Checks
The top security card is revealed. If the card was already revealed, it remains revealed.
Processing for effects triggered upon a security check
If an effect is triggered by a security check, that effect is to be resolved. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action.
Processing Battles against Security Digimon

A battle will occur between the Security Digimon and the Digimon that performed the security check. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")
If a Security Digimon isn't present, proceed to the next step.
A card revealed from a security check is placed in the trash unless it belongs to an area.
If the card performing the security check can perform another security check, it will then perform that security check.
Battles
A "battle" refers to comparing the DP of the two battling cards.
The processing for a battle is performed using the following procedure.
The DP values of the two battling cards are compared.
The card with the higher DP is the winner.
The card with the lower DP loses.
If both cards have the same DP, both lose the battle.
The Digimon that loses is immediately deleted. If both lose, both are deleted at the same time.
Security Digimon aren't deleted even when they lose a battle.
If an effect is triggered by a battle, that effect is to be resolved. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action.
If an effect is triggered by the end of the battle timing when a battle ends, that effect is to be resolved.
Effect Rules
Effects
An effect refers to the processing activated by a card that affects the game or cards themselves.

A single effect is processed in the order shown in the text on the card. However, if that single effect has optional processing conditions that affect it, decide whether or not to perform them before processing the effect.

A prohibiting effect takes precedence over an enabling effect. (Example: A Digimon with a "[Your Turn] This Digimon can also attack your opponent's unsuspended Digimon" effect can't attack an unsuspended Digimon with an "[Opponent's Turn] This Digimon can't be attacked" effect.)
In some cases, multiple processes will be performed in a single effect. Once all of the processes for such an effect have ended, the effect will be resolved.
If an effect is mandatory and not optional, its processing must be performed whenever possible.
The processing to execute is chosen, then the processing is executed for the effect. Once the processing to execute is chosen, the effect is considered to be activated.

If an effect doesn't specify an area, it means that it can specify or reference a card in the battle area, or that it can affect the battle area. (Example: "[On Play] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with <Blocker>" is an effect where you specify 1 of your opponent's Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area to be deleted.)
Effects that specify or reference Security Digimon can specify, reference, or affect Security Digimon.

If an effect's trigger conditions or processing conditions include placing a card in an area other than the field, the conditions will be met even if the card isn't actually placed in that area due to Digi-Egg card or token rules.

If an effect's trigger conditions or processing conditions include a card being added to an area other than the field, the trigger conditions won't be met by a Digi-Egg or token because the card isn't actually placed in that area due to Digi-Egg card or token rules.
Effect Types
Effects are divided into the following types.
An effect activated by a Digimon card, Digimon, or Security Digimon is considered a Digimon effect.
An effect activated by a Tamer card or Tamer is considered a Tamer effect.
An effect activated by an Option card is considered an Option card effect.
Inherited Effects
An inherited effect is an effect gained by a Digimon from a digivolution card. This effect can't be activated by just 1 card.

An inherited effect gained by a Digimon is considered an effect activated by a Digimon regardless of the digivolution card's card category. Therefore, the effect type for these effects is considered to be Digimon effects.
Even if a card is stacked on top of a Digimon, inherited effects gained by it will be carried over along with their states at that point in time.
If "this card" is specified in an inherited effect, that inherited effect is considered to be triggered and activated by that card itself that is or was in digivolution cards.
Effect States
Activation
Activation refers to an effect being executed.

When a card activates an effect, all of the effect is resolved, even if that card becomes a new card during the processing for the activated effect. (Example: If your Digimon has "[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less and return 1 of their level 6 or higher Digimon to the bottom of the deck," when you delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less, you will process "return 1 of their level 6 or higher Digimon to the bottom of the deck," even if another immedia te-type effect deletes your Digimon.)
Triggering
Triggering refers to when the conditions have been met for an effect to trigger. Some effects activate without triggering.
When an effect's trigger conditions are met during a game, it will trigger no matter the circumstances, even when processing is being performed for a rule or effect.
Effects that are pending activation must be activated 1 at a time. Multiple triggered effects can't be activated at the same time.
If an already triggered effect's trigger conditions are met again before it activates, that effect will be triggered again.
Simultaneous Triggering
Simultaneous triggering refers to when multiple effects trigger at the same timing.

If multiple effects are triggered before a single rule or effect is resolved, they all trigger simultaneously. If effects trigger simultaneously, the effects will be pending activation and activate 1 at a time. (For details, refer to 15-4-4 "Pending Activation") 15-4-

When an effect is triggered by a rule check, it triggers simultaneously with other effects that triggered at that timing. (Example: An [On Deletion] effect on a Digimon that was deleted by its DP becoming 0 at the start of your turn will trigger simultaneously with [Start of Your Turn] effects.)
The activation order is determined for effects that trigger simultaneously by choosing the next pending activation effect after each effect has been resolved.
Effects that trigger simultaneously are processed by performing the following procedure.

The turn player chooses 1 of their effects to activate from among the effects that triggered simultaneously. This step is repeated until there are no more pending activation effects for the turn player.

Once there are no more pending activation effects for the turn player, the non-turn player chooses 1 of their effects to activate from among the effects that triggered simultaneously. This step is repeated until there are no more pending activation effects for the non-turn player.
Pending Activation
Pending activation refers to the period until a triggered effect activates.
Effects that are pending activation must be activated 1 at a time. Multiple triggered effects can't be activated at the same time.

When a card with an effect that's pending activation becomes a new card before the effect activates, the effect can no longer be activated. (Example: When an [On Play] effect is triggered by a card being played, if the card is removed from the battle area before the effect is activated, the effect can no longer be activated.)

When a card with an effect that's pending activation loses the effect before it activates, the effect can no longer be activated. (Example: When a Digimon with the text "[When Attacking] <Draw 1>" and "[When Attacking] This Digimon may digivolve into a Digimon card with the [Hybrid] trait in the hand with the digivolution cost reduced by 1" attacks, then it digivolves from the 2nd [When Attacking] effect, the 1st [When Attacking] effect can no longer activate.)
When a card with an effect that's pending activation no longer meets the trigger conditions of that effect before it activates, the effect can no longer be activated.
Derived Triggering
Derived triggering refers to an effect that newly triggers while simultaneously triggered effects are still resolving. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
A derived triggering effect will activate before previously triggered effects that are pending activation.
If a derived triggering effect occurs for the non-turn player when there are pending activation effects for the turn player, the derived triggering effect will activate first.
Trigger Conditions

Trigger conditions are the conditions for an effect to trigger. As soon as the trigger conditions are met, that effect will trigger. Trigger conditions include timings when an effect would trigger such as "when [...] would" text.

A triggering from 1 trigger condition is considered to only trigger once, even if it occurred multiple times at the same time. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When a card is removed from your security stack, <De-Digivolve 1> 1 of your opponent's Digimon" will only trigger once, even if 2 or more cards are trashed from your security stack at the same time.)

If an effect's trigger conditions are met as soon as a card is placed in an area where they can trigger, that effect will trigger. Example: If a card has a "[Your Turn] [Once Per Turn] When your effect places a digivolution card under this Digimon, gain 1 memory" inherited effect, the trigger conditions will be met even when that card itself is placed in digivolution cards by one of your effects.)
Processing Conditions

When processing has processing conditions, its text will show the conditions for processing the effect. The processing can be executed when those conditions are met. Processing conditions include text such as "if" or "while". (Example: "While this Digimon is suspended" is a processing condition in an "[All Turns] While this Digimon is suspended, this Digimon gets +3000 DP" effect.)

A processing condition is a condition for a process to be performed after text such as "if" or "while." Different processes in the same effect don't have to meet the processing conditions for other processes. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] If you have 1 or fewer Tamers, you may play 1 [Kiriha Aonuma] from your hand without paying the cost. Then, <Save>," <Save> can be processed even if you have 2 or more Tamers.)

An effect can't be activated when none of its processing conditions are met. (Example: An effect that reads "[When Digivolving] If you don't have [Marcus Damon], you may play 1 [Marcus Damon] from your hand without paying the cost" can't be activated when you have [Marcus Damon] in the battle area.)
Optional Processing Conditions

If an effect has optional processing conditions, its text will show the conditions for processing the effect. If the player chooses to execute the processing for the conditions and is successful, the processing after the conditions is performed. Optional processing conditions include text such as "by X, Y." (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] By trashing 1 card in the hand, gain 1 memory," The "by trashing 1 card in the hand" part is an optional processing condition.

If the content of the optional processing conditions isn't executed, the processing after the conditions can't be executed. (Examples: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] By trashing 2 cards in your hand, this Digimon unsuspends. After, if [WereGarurumon] or [X Antibody] is in this Digimon's digivolution cards, you may return 1 Digimon card with [Garurumon] or [X Antibody] in its name from your trash to the hand," unless the player trashes 2 cards in their hand, "this Digimon unsuspends" and the content after "After" can't be executed.)

It isn't possible to only perform some of the optional processing conditions. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] By returning 1 [Kimeramon] and 1 [Machinedramon] from your trash to the bottom of the deck, you may play 1 [Millenniummon] from your trash without paying the cost," a player can't just return 1 [Kimeramon] or 1 [Machinedramon] to the bottom of their deck.

If executing an optional processing condition's contents isn't possible, then the player can't choose to execute them. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] By trashing your top security card, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets-5000 DP for the turn," and the player doesn't have even 1 security card, then they can't choose to execute that condition's contents.)

A player can choose to execute the content of optional processing conditions, regardless of whether or not the content after the conditions can be executed. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] By trashing your top security card, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets - 5000 DP for the turn," a player can choose to trash their top security card even when the opponent doesn't have any Digimon in the battle area.)
Effect Categories
Effect categories include persistent, trigger-type, activation-type, and immediate-type.
Persistent Effects

Persistent effects are constantly activated without being triggered. This refers to effects with text such as "[Your Turn] This Digimon gets +1000 DP" that don't have any particular trigger timings shown.

Persistent effects are constantly activated as soon as their activation conditions are met. (Examples: If a Tamer card has an effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your Digimon get +1000 DP," the effect will be constantly activated as soon as your turn begins.)

Persistent effects won't be activated as soon as their activation conditions are no longer met. (Examples: If a Tamer card has an effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your Digimon get +1000 DP," the effect will no longer be activated as soon as the opponent's turn begins.)
When multiple persistent effects are activated, they all overlap.
If multiple persistent effects with conflicting content are activated, effects that activate afterward take priority, except prohibiting effects.
Persistent Effects With Processing Conditions
Persistent effects with processing conditions will be constantly activated while their processing conditions are met.
Persistent effects with processing conditions won't be activated as soon as their processing conditions are no longer met.
Trigger-Type Effects

A trigger-type effect will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect will activate. If an effect reads "[When Attacking] Lose 2 memory" or "[Your Turn] When effects suspend this Digimon, suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon," that shows a trigger timing.
Trigger-type effects can't activate during the processing for a rule or effect.
A trigger-type effect will trigger when the specific conditions are met for the effect on that card to trigger.
Trigger-type effects won't trigger when their trigger conditions aren't met.

If a trigger-type effect triggers when a card is deleted, the card where it will be pending activation is the card that was the top card in the original area. (Example: Upon the deletion of a Digimon with an inherited effect that reads "[On Deletion] Gain 1 memory" on its digivolution card, that effect will trigger, and it will be pending activation for the card that was the top card of that Digimon.)

If a trigger-type effect triggers at the end of the turn timing, it will trigger as soon as the end of the turn timing arrives. Once an effect triggers, it will remain triggered, even if the memory increases or decreases.

If an unspecified reference is to be made during the processing for a trigger-type effect, the reference is made in the state when the processing is being performed. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When a card is added to your security stack, return 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a level less than or equal to the number of your security cards to the hand," if you have 4 security cards when referencing them for the processing, you would return 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon to the hand.)

If a reference in the same state as the effect's trigger conditions is to be made during the processing for a trigger-type effect, the state where the effect has triggered will be referenced. The state where the effect has triggered will be referenced, even if the state changes after the effect triggers. This refers to effects where text such as "when another of your Digimon is played" is a trigger condition and a reference is made using text such as "Digimon with a level less than or equal to the played Di gimon." (Example: When an effect plays a level 4 Digimon and an effect reads "[All Turns] When an effect plays another of your Digimon, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a level less than or equal to the played Digimon," this effect deletes 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon, even if the Digimon digivolves into a level 5 Digimon before this effect activates.)
Trigger-Type Effects With Processing Conditions
A trigger-type effect with processing conditions will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect will activate if the processing conditions are met.

Trigger-type effects will trigger if their trigger conditions are met, regardless of whether or not their processing conditions are met. However, the processing conditions must be met at the time of activation in order for the effect to activate.

If a reference is to be made in the processing conditions for a trigger-type effect, the reference is made in the state when the processing is being performed. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] When your opponent plays a Digimon, by suspending this Tamer, if that Digimon is level 4 or higher, gain 1 memory. If it is level 3, <Draw 1>," you will gain 1 memory if your opponent's Digimon is level 4 upon being referenced when this effect activates.)

If a reference is to be made in the processing conditions for a trigger-type effect that will trigger when a card is removed from an area, the reference is made in the state when the effect triggered. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] When this Digimon has digivolution cards, you may play this card from your trash without paying the cost," it references whether or not that Digimon has digivolution cards upon deletion.)
Activation-Type Effects

Activation-type effects are effects that can be optionally activated by a player. These include effects with [Main] text such as "[Main] [Once Per Turn] By paying 2 cost, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with DP less than or equal to this Digimon’s DP."
Activation-type effects can be activated during your main phase by declaring their activation when there is no unresolved processing.
Activation-Type Effects With Processing Conditions
A player can only declare activation of an activation-type effect while its processing conditions are met.
Activation-Type Effects With Optional Processing Conditions

If an activation-type effect has optional processing conditions, a player can only declare activation while the optional processing conditions can be performed. In addition, once declared, the optional processing conditions must be performed. (Example: Activation of <Training> can be declared if suspending is possible. Once declared, suspending must be performed.)
Immediate-Type Effects

An immediate-type effect will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect can be activated. However, these effects will interrupt right before the cause of a rule or effect, unlike trigger-type effects. These include effects with "when X would" or "when X would be removed" in their text, such as "[Your Turn] When this Digimon would digivolve into a card with [Greymon] in its name, reduce the digivolution cost by 1 for each color on that card."

Activation of immediate-type effects will interrupt right before the cause of such effects. (Example: An immediate-type effect that triggers "when X would be deleted" will trigger immediately before the deletion, and if that "when X would be deleted" effect prevents the card from being removed from the battle area, it isn't deleted.)
Immediate-type effects will only trigger simultaneously with other immediate-type effects.

Each immediate-type effect can be activated once until the event that first triggered the immediate-type effect is resolved. (Example: If "[Main] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon" causes "[All Turns] When this Digimon would be deleted, by deleting 1 other Digimon with [Sukamon] in its name, it isn't deleted" to activate, until the deletion is resolved, the already activated "[All Turns] When this Digimon would be deleted, by deleting 1 other Digimon with [Sukamon] in its name, it isn't deleted" can't activate again.)
Immediate-Type Effects With Processing Conditions
An immediate-type effect with processing conditions will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect can be activated if its processing conditions are met.
Even if an immediate-type effect with processing conditions triggers when its processing conditions aren't met, it can be activated if its processing conditions are later met.
Mandatory Processing and Optional Processing
Mandatory Processing
Mandatory processing refers to text whose action is required.
The player must choose to execute the content of mandatory processing. A player can't choose to not execute it.
Optional Processing
Optional processing refers to text whose action is optional.
The player can choose to execute the content of optional processing.
Effect Targets
Effect Targets - Players
"You" or "Your"
If text includes "you" or "your," it affects the player of that card.
"Opponent"
If text includes "opponent," it affects the opponent player.
"Both Players"
If text includes "players" or "both players," it affects both players.
Effect Targets - Cards

If text such as "X Digimon" or "X cards" is written on a card, X number of cards or as many cards up to X as possible must be chosen. The individual processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-1 "Individual Processing")

If text such as "up to X Digimon" or "up to X cards" is written on a card, up to X number of cards are chosen. The individual processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-1 "Individual Processing")

When multiple cards are to be chosen at the same time, the same target card can't be chosen multiple times. (Example: If an effect reads "[Main] 3 of your opponent's Digimon get-5000 DP and <Security Attack-1> until the end of their turn," the same Digimon can't be chosen 3 times.)
"All"
When "all" is specified, the target cards aren't chosen. Overall processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-2 "Overall Processing") 15-11-2
Individual Processing and Overall Processing
Individual Processing

Individual processing refers to when a target is chosen for processing. Individual processing affects the chosen target. This refers to processing where a target is chosen, including text such as "[Main] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets-7000 DP for the turn."
If the chosen card for individual processing becomes a new card, that individual processing will be lost. (For details, refer to 3-1-3-1 "New Cards")
Individual Processing With Conditions for Choosing a Target

When individual processing has conditions for choosing a target, only a target that meets those conditions can be chosen. This refers to processing with conditions for choosing a target including effects such as "[Main] Choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards. That Digimon can't attack or block until the end of your opponent's next turn."

When a target is affected by an effect where individual processing has conditions for choosing a target, the effect will continue affecting the target, even if the target no longer meets the conditions after being affected. (Example: If a Digimon is affected by an effect such as "[Main] Choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards. That Digimon can't attack or block until the end of your opponent's next turn," that Digimon can't attack even if it later gets a digivolution card.)
Overall Processing

Overall processing refers to when a target isn't chosen for processing. Overall processing affects cards overall. This refers to processing where a target isn't chosen, including effects with text such as "[On Play] [When Digivolving] All of your opponent's Digimon get-5000 DP for the turn."

Overall processing that is continuous will also affect targets that are added later. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] [On Deletion] All of your opponent's Digimon get-5000 DP for the turn," Digimon placed in the battle area after this effect activates will also get-5000 DP.)
Overall Processing With Conditions for Affecting Targets

When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, the processing affects all of the targets that meet those conditions. This refers to processing with conditions for affecting targets including effects such as "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block."

When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, as soon as a target no longer meets the conditions after being affected, the processing will no longer affect that target. (Example: While an effect that reads "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block" is activated, an opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can't attack or block, but if it later gets a digivolution card, it will then be able to attack or block.)

When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, as soon as a target that wasn't affected meets the conditions, the processing will affect that target. (Example: While an effect that reads "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block" is activated, an opponent's Digimon with digivolution cards can attack or block, but if it later has no digivolution cards, it will no longer be able to attack or block.)
Effects That Add Information and Effects That Change Information
Effects That Add Information

"Effects that add information" refers to effects that add information to a card. These include effects such as "[Main] [Once Per Turn] 1 of your [Marcus Damon] is treated as a 3000 DP Digimon that can't digivolve for the turn."
Effects that add information can also add information that a card didn't already have.

An effect that adds information can only add to the play cost, level, or DP of 1 card at a time. If an effect adds information to a card that already has such information, the newly added information will overwrite the previous information. An effect that adds information can only add to the play cost, level, or DP of 1 card at a time. If an effect adds information to a card that already has such information, the newly added information will overwrite the previous information. However, if the same information has already been added by a persistent effect, that effect will always overwrite the information. If the persistent effect is lost, the information will return to the previous state.
If an effect that adds information treats a card as a Digimon, the rules for Digimon will also apply to that card. (For details, refer to 4-2 "Digimon")
If an effect that adds information adds DP to a card that didn't originally have DP, the added DP will be treated as that card's original DP.

If an effect that adds information causes a card to be treated as both a Digimon and a Tamer card, an effect activated by that card will be considered both a Digimon effect and a Tamer effect. (Example: When an "[All Turns] Your opponent can't gain memory other than by Tamer effects" effect is activated, the effects of a Tamer that is also treated as a Digimon will still be considered to be Tamer effects, therefore its effects can still gain memory.)
Effects That Change Information

"Effects that change information" refers to effects that change the information on a card. These include effects such as "[Security] Change the original name of 1 of your opponent's Digimon to [Sukamon] (white/3000 DP) until the end of your turn."
Effects that change information can't change information that a card didn't originally have.

If an effect changes information on a card that has already been affected by an effect that changes information, the most recently changed information will overwrite the previous information. However, if the same information is changed by a persistent effect, that effect will always overwrite the information. If the persistent effect is lost, the information will return to the previous state.
Gained Effects
Some effects can be gained through other effects.
When an effect is gained, the effect and the state of the effect at that time will be carried over, even if a card is placed on top of that card or a card is removed from its stack.

If the gained effect is triggered by the card itself being deleted, that effect's state will be carried over even after being placed into the trash by deletion. (Example: If a Digimon gaining an [On Deletion] effect from an effect is deleted, that gained [On Deletion] effect becomes pending activation even if it is placed into the trash.)
Effect Icons
[X Per Turn]
[X Per Turn] means that an effect can be activated a number of times during 1 turn as specified by X, and each activation counts toward 1 use of X.
If an [X Per Turn] effect is used X number of times during 1 turn, it won't trigger again during that turn.
The uses of an [X Per Turn] effect are counted individually for each copy of a card.
When a player chooses to activate an [X Per Turn] effect, it will count toward 1 use of [X Per Turn], even if the effect's processing can't be executed.
The number of uses for an [X Per Turn] effect will be reset in the following circumstances.
The turn changed.
The card with that effect is considered to become a new card. (For details, refer to 3-1-3-1 "New Cards")
{Hand}
An effect with the {Hand} icon can be activated when you reveal the card with the effect from your hand.
{Trash}
An effect with the {Trash} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is in your trash.
{Breeding}
An effect with the {Breeding} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is in the breeding area.
{Security}
An effect with the {Security} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is placed face-up in the security stack.
Rules for Effect Text
Effects That End an Attack
If an attack is ended by an effect, the end of attack timing comes immediately after the processing for that effect.
"Gains"
"Gains" means that a target card gains an effect.
When a target gains an effect, it is affected by that effect.
Effects That Let Players View Cards

Letting players view a card doesn't count as adding to or removing from the card's original area. However, a card that's being viewed is not treated as being in its original area. (Example: Revealing your security cards does not cause "when your security stack is removed from" effects to trigger. Also, when trashing cards that have been revealed from the deck, those cards are not treated as having been trashed from the deck.)

When cards being viewed are added to or removed from, it is treated as adding to or removing from the viewed cards' original area. (Example: Trashing cards that are being revealed from the security stack causes "when your security stack is removed from" effects to trigger.)
When all cards in an area are being viewed, other effects can't add cards to that area.

Letting players view cards is treated as a single action until all of the viewed cards have been placed in an area. (Example: The effect "[On Play] Reveal the top 5 cards of your deck. Add 1 Tamer card among them to the hand. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck" is treated as a single action once all the remaining cards have been returned to the bottom of the deck.)

If a card needs to be drawn while cards from the deck are being viewed, the card is drawn from the non-viewed cards. (Example: When digivolving with the effect "[When Attacking] Reveal the top 3 cards of your deck. This Digimon may digivolve into 1 green level 6 Digimon card among them without paying the cost. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck", the digivolution bonus card is drawn from the cards in the deck that aren't being revealed.)

When multiple cards are returned to their original state while being viewed, the player whose card caused the action chooses the order of those cards. (Example: When returning multiple cards to the bottom of the deck at the same time with the effect "[On Play] Reveal the top 4 cards of your deck. Add 1 card with [Gammamon] in its text among them to the hand. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck", the player who activated the effect chooses the order they are returned in.))
Effects that let players view cards have 2 types: "Reveal" and "search"/"look at."
Revealing Cards
"Revealing" one or more cards means to reveal them to both players.
"Search"/"Look At"
"Searching" an area or "looking at" certain cards refers to cards that are only revealed to a specific player.

If a player isn't specified in text, only the player that activated the effect searches/looks at the cards. However, when searching/looking at cards in the hand, they are revealed to both their owner and the player who is searching/looking at them.

After searching an area or looking at cards, the cards are returned according to the rules for the respective area. If searching/looking at is followed by processing, perform it after the cards are returned.
Effects that add or reduce an effect's numerical value
An effect that adds to the numerical value of an effect will add to the value shown in text.
An effect that reduces the numerical value of an effect will reduce the value shown in text.

Effects that add or reduce an effect's numerical value can't add or reduce a numerical value that isn't shown in text for an effect. (Example: A "[Your Turn] Add 1000 to the maximum your DP-based deletion effects can delete" effect can't add to the maximum of a "[When Attacking] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with DP less than or equal to this Digimon's DP" effect.
"Isn't affected by effects" cards

When a card isn't affected by effects, it won't be affected by processing caused by effects. (Example: Even if a card that isn't affected by effects is chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, it isn't suspended.)

When a card isn't affected by effects, then it can be affected again, effects will immediately start affecting that card. (Example: When a-3000 DP effect is applied to a suspended Digimon with an "[All Turns] While this Digimon is suspended, this Digimon isn't affected by the effects of your opponent's Digimon" effect, the Digimon will get - 3000 DP as soon as it's unsuspended.)

"Isn't affected by effects" cards can still be chosen for effects. (Example: A card that isn't affected by effects can be chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, but it isn't affected by that effect and it isn't suspended.)

Even if a Digimon that isn't affected by effects gains an effect, the Digimon won't be considered to have that effect. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gains <Security A. -1> until the end of their turn," even if a Digimon that isn't affected by effects gains <Security A. -1>, the Digimon won't be considered to have <Security A. -1>.
Effects That Can Replace DigiXros Requirements
Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements allow cards to replace those shown in brackets in the DigiXros requirement text.

Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements can't replace DigiXros requirements that specify a card that isn't the same as another. (Example: Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements can't replace a card for "∞ Digimon cards w/[Xros Heart] or [Blue Flare] trait & different card numbers.")
Effects That Activate Other Effects

During the processing of effects that activate other effects, another effect will activate and process. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] You may place 1 card with [Royal Knight] in its traits and a play cost of 13 or less from your hand or trash under this Digimon as its bottom digivolution card. Activate 1 of that card's [When Digivolving] effects as an effect of this Digimon. Then, <Blitz>," a [When Digivolving] effect on the card placed as the bottom digivolution card will activate, then <Blitz> will be processed after that effect is processed.

If multiple other effects will activate, the player can activate them one at a time in the order they choose. If multiple types of effects can be activated, choose one and activate it before choosing the next one, and repeat this process the number of times specified. (Example: If "[When Attacking] Activate 1 of the effects below. If you have no other Digimon in play, activate all of the effects below instead" is used to activate all of the other effects, the player can choose their activation order.)
If an effect that activates another effect has text such as "activate as this card's effect," the card that activated this effect will be considered to have activated the effect.

Even if the effect activating another effect is mandatory, the player can still choose whether or not to processes that other effect's optional processing conditions. (Example: When activating another effect with the effect "[When Attacking] [Once Per Turn] Activate 1 [On Play] effect on a face-up [Zaxon] trait Digimon card in your security stack as an effect of this Digimon" and that other effect has optional processing conditions, the player can choose whether or not to process them.)
Effect Timings
Effect timings are shown using text in icons enclosed in brackets.
[On Play]
[On Play] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the action of playing a card with that effect is complete.
[When Digivolving]
[When Digivolving] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the action of digivolving into a card with that effect is complete.
[On Deletion]
[On Deletion] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect is deleted.
[When Attacking]
[When Attacking] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when an attack declaration is made for the card with that effect.
[When Linking]
[When Linking] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect becomes a link card.
[Main]
[Main] is an effect timing for activation-type effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-4 "Activation - Type Effects")
[Your Turn] and [Opponent's Turn]
[Your Turn] and [Opponent's Turn] are timings where effects can be triggered and activated during the respective turns shown in text.
[All Turns]
[All Turns] is an effect timing where effects can be triggered and activated during both your turns and your opponent's turns.
[Security]
[Security] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when a security check is performed on the card with that effect.

A triggered [Security] effect will immediately activate without pending activation. Therefore, [Security] effects take precedence for activation even when they trigger simultaneously with other effects.
[Start of Your Turn] and [Start of Opponent's Turn]

[Start of Your Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your unsuspend phase has arrived. The effects trigger and activate before the unsuspending actions in the unsuspend phase.

[Start of Opponent's Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's unsuspend phase has arrived. The effects trigger and activate before the unsuspending actions in the unsuspend phase.
[End of Your Turn], [End of Opponent's Turn], and [End of All Turns]
[End of Your Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your turn ends.
[End of Opponent's Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's turn ends.
[End of All Turns] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when a turn ends for all players.
[Start of Your Main Phase] and [Start of Opponent's Main Phase]
[Start of Your Main Phase] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your main phase has arrived.
[Start of Opponent's Main Phase] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's main phase has arrived.
[Counter]
[Counter] is an effect timing for special activation-type effects. (For details, refer to 11-3 "Counter Timing")
[End of Attack]
[End of Attack] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the end of the attack arrives after an attack is performed using the card with that effect.
[When Moving]
[When Moving] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect is moved.
Keyword Effects
Keyword effects are effects indicated by icons enclosed in brackets.
A keyword effect is considered to be the same type even if it has a different numerical value or specified card included in the icon enclosed in brackets.
"Specified cards" for a keyword effect refers to the cards that meet the conditions shown in parentheses for icons that use angle brackets.
<Security A.> (※formerly <Security Attack>)

<Security A.> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect will have a modified number of security checks according to the number specified for this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Security A. +1>.

<Security A.> effects are persistent effects. The number of security checks is modified as soon as the effect is applied. (Example: If a Digimon gained <Security A. +1> at the point when it performs a security check, it will perform 1 additional security check.) (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

If 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Security A.>, the number of security checks that can be performed is modified according to their numerical values. However, even if a card has multiple instances of <Security A.>, the effect isn't considered to be an effect with the combined values from <Security A.>. (Examples: If a Digimon has 2 instances of <Security A. +1>, the additional number of cards checked will be 2, but the Digimon isn't considered to have <Security A. +2>.)
Even if a negative value is the result of the number of security checks being modified, the actual number of security checks is 0.
<Blocker>
<Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
<Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.
<Recovery>
<Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.
<Recovery> effects execute processing.
<Piercing>

<Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")

<Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.

<Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)

Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.
<Draw>
<Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
<Draw> effects execute processing.
A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.
<Jamming>
<Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.
<Jamming> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Digisorption>

<Digisorption> is a keyword effect. When a digivolution into a Digimon card with this effect in the hand would occur, by suspending 1 of your Digimon, the digivolution cost is reduced according to the value specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digisorption-3>.
<Digisorption> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when a digivolution into a card with this effect in the hand would occur. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

"By suspending 1 of your Digimon" in <Digisorption> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "the digivolution cost is reduced" will be mandatory.
If 1 Digimon card has multiple instances of <Digisorption>, they overlap when they trigger. Multiple instances of <Digisorption> can be activated for a single digivolution.
<Digisorption> can be used to suspend a Digimon that will become a digivolution card.
<Reboot>
<Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
<Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
The unsuspending from <Reboot> is mandatory.
The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.
<De-Digivolve>

<De-Digivolve> is a keyword effect where the player declares a number from 1 up to the number specified in the effect, then the declared number of cards are trashed from the chosen stack(s) of cards starting with the top card. This is shown on cards using text such as <De - Digivolve 1>.
<De-Digivolve> effects execute processing.
The trashing from <De-Digivolve> is mandatory. Once activated, a player can't choose to trash 0 cards.
<De-Digivolve> can't trash cards from level 3 cards or lower.

If multiple cards are trashed using 1 instance of <De - Digivolve>, all of the cards are considered to be trashed at the same time, but the procedure for trashing them is 1 card from the stack at a time.

When using <De-Digivolve> to trash multiple cards, even if the category of the top card changes while the trashing is still being performed, the trashing will continue until the declared number is trashed.
When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the processing is performed separately for each instance.

When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the state of the chosen card is confirmed after each single process for <De-Digivolve> ends. If an effect will be activated as a result of the confirmed state, it is then activated. (Example: When 3 instances of <De-Digivolve 1> are executed in a single effect, if the chosen card becomes an "unaffected by effects" card as a result of the 1st instance of <De-Digivolve 1>, that card is unaffected by the following instances of <De-Digivolve 1>.
<Retaliation>
<Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.
<Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Retaliation> is mandatory.
<Digi-Burst>

<Digi-Burst> is a keyword effect where another effect specified by this effect will activate by trashing the specified number of digivolution cards from the Digimon with this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digi-Burst 1>.
The processing from <Digi-Burst> is optional. For details, refer to 15-6 "Processing Conditions")
<Rush>
<Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.
<Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Blitz>
<Blitz> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect can attack if your opponent has 1 or more memory.
<Blitz> effects execute processing.
<Blitz> has a processing condition that requires the memory to be at 1 or more on your opponent's side. "This Digimon may attack" is optional processing.
After using <Blitz> to make an attack declaration, the attack will proceed even if the memory moves to 0 or more.
An attack can't be made using <Blitz> if the memory is at 0 or more upon activating <Blitz>.
<Delay>
<Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.
The processing from <Delay> is optional. (For details, refer to 15-7 "Optional Processing Conditions")
<Delay> can't be activated the same turn the card with the effect is placed in the battle area.
<Decoy>

<Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.

<Decoy> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when another of your Digimon specified by this effect would be deleted by an opponent's effect (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

"By deleting this Digimon" in <Decoy> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "<Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted" will be mandatory.
<Armor Purge>
<Armor Purge> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with <Armor Purge> would be deleted, by trashing the top card of the Digimon with this effect, this effect prevents the deletion.
<Armor Purge> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

"By trashing the top card of the Digimon" in <Armor Purge> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
<Save>
<Save> is a keyword effect that allows you to place this card under 1 of your Tamers.
<Save> effects execute processing.
The processing from <Save> is optional.
<Material Save>

<Material Save> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted, this effect allows you to place a number of the cards specified in the top card's DigiXros requirements from among the digivolution cards under 1 of your Tamers. The number of cards placed is the number specified in this keyword effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Material Save 1>.
<Material Save> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
The processing from <Material Save> is optional. However, if <Material Save> will be processed, the number of cards specified by this effect must be placed under your Tamer whenever possible.

When multiple cards would be placed under 1 Tamer for 1 instance of <Material Save>, the procedure for placing them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time. In addition, the placement order is chosen by the player processing <Material Save>.

As long as you use a card specified in the DigiXros requirements, multiple copies of the same card can be placed under the Tamer for <Material Save>. (Example: If a Digimon with <Material Save 2> has [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]×[Dorulumon] in its DigiXros requirements, 2 copies of [Shoutmon] can be placed under the Tamer.)
If there are any cards stacked under the Tamer when processing <Material Save>, the new card is placed at the bottom.
<Evade>
<Evade> is a keyword effect. By suspending a Digimon with this effect when it would be deleted, this effect prevents the deletion.
<Evade> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
"By suspending a Digimon with this effect" in <Evade> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
<Raid>
<Raid> is a keyword effect that can switch the target of attack to the opponent's unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when a Digimon with this keyword effect attacks.
<Raid> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Raid> is optional.

If the opponent has multiple unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when <Raid> activates, the player that activated the effect chooses a Digimon from among them and the attack target is switched to it.
<Alliance>

<Alliance> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack.
<Alliance> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")

"By suspending 1 of your other Digimon" in <Alliance> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "when a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack" will be mandatory.
The value added to DP by <Alliance> is the value of the suspended Digimon upon the suspension. The added DP from <Alliance> isn't modified, even if the DP of your suspended Digimon is later modified.
Even if your Digimon that was suspended by <Alliance> is removed from the battle area during the attack, the added DP and <Security A. +1> remain.
<Barrier>
<Barrier> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle, by trashing the top card of your security stack, this effect prevents that deletion.
<Barrier> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

"By trashing the top card of your security stack" in <Barrier> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
<Blast Digivolve>
<Blast Digivolve> is a keyword effect that allows one of your Digimon to digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost.
<Blast Digivolve> effects execute processing.
The processing from <Blast Digivolve> is optional.
<Blast Digivolve> is an effect that digivolves the chosen Digimon in the battle area.
<Fortitude>
<Fortitude> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted, you play this Digimon without paying the cost.
<Fortitude> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Fortitude> is mandatory.
<Mind Link>
<Mind Link> is a keyword effect that places a Tamer with this effect in the digivolution cards of a Digimon with no Tamer cards in its digivolution cards.
<Mind Link> effects execute processing.
The processing from <Mind Link> is mandatory. However, if it uses the [Main] activation timing, it can be activated and processed at a timing chosen by the player.
<Partition>

<Partition> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle, you may play 1 of each of the specified cards from the digivolution cards without paying their costs. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Partition (blue Lv.4 & green Lv.4)>."

<Partition> is an immediate-type effect that triggers "when a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle." (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
The processing from <Partition> is optional.
When <Partition> is activated, 1 of each of the specified cards is played from digivolution cards without paying their costs. A player can't choose to only play one or some of the specified cards.
<Collision>

<Collision> is a keyword effect. While a Digimon with this effect is attacking, all of your opponent's Digimon gain <Blocker> and the opponent player is forced to block whenever possible during the block timing.
<Collision> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Collision> will activate while the Digimon with this effect is attacking.

"All of your opponent's Digimon gain <Blocker>" in <Collision> is processing that affects Digimon. "The opponent player is forced to block whenever possible" is processing that affects the opponent player.
<Blast DNA Digivolve>

<Blast DNA Digivolve> is a keyword effect. One of your Digimon specified in this effect and a card from your hand may digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Blast DNA Digivolve> <[Durandamon] + [BryweLudramon]>."
<Blast DNA Digivolve> effects execute processing.
The processing from <Blast DNA Digivolve> is optional.
<Blast DNA Digivolve> is an effect that performs DNA digivolution. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")
A Digimon card's DNA digivolution requirements can't be ignored for <Blast DNA Digivolve>.

When DNA digivolution is performed using <Blast DNA Digivolve>, the player reveals the cards that will become digivolution cards from their hand at the same time as when they choose their Digimon that meet the DNA digivolution requirements.
<Scapegoat>
<Scapegoat> is a keyword effect. By deleting 1 of your other Digimon when a Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects, this effect prevents the deletion.
<Scapegoat> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
"By deleting 1 of your other Digimon" in <Scapegoat> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
<Vortex>
<Vortex> allows the Digimon with this effect to attack an opponent's Digimon at the end of your turn. <Vortex> is a keyword effect that also allows a Digimon to attack in the same turn it was played.
<Vortex> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the end of your turn. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Vortex> is optional.
<Overclock>

<Overclock> is a keyword effect. At the end of your turn, by deleting 1 of your Tokens or 1 of your other specified Digimon, the Digimon with this effect attacks a player without suspending. This is shown on cards using text such as <Overclock ([Puppet] Trait)>.
<Overclock> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the end of your turn. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")

"By deleting 1 of your Tokens or 1 of your other specified Digimon" in <Overclock> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "the Digimon with this effect attacks a player without suspending" will be mandatory.
<Iceclad>
<Iceclad> is a keyword effect where you compare the number of digivolution cards instead of DP when you battle using the Digimon with this effect, other than battles against Security Digimon.
<Iceclad> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Iceclad> is an effect that changes the rules of a battle.
When using <Iceclad> to compare the number of digivolution cards for two cards in a battle, the winner and loser of the battle are determined as follows.
The card with the higher number of digivolution cards is the winner.
The card with the lower number of digivolution cards is the loser.
If both have the same number of digivolution cards, both cards lose the battle.
<Decode>

<Decode> is a keyword effect. When the Digimon with this effect would leave the battle area other than by a battle, you may play 1 specified Digimon card from that Digimon's digivolution cards without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Decode (blue Lv.4)>."
<Decode> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would leave the battle area other than by a battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
The processing from <Decode> is optional.
<Fragment>

<Fragment> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted, by choosing and trashing the specified number of this Digimon's digivolution cards, it isn't deleted. The effect is indicated on cards by icons such as <Fragment (3)>.
<Fragment> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

The processing from <Fragment> for choosing and trashing the specified number of this Digimon's digivolution cards is optional. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
<Execute>

<Execute> is a keyword effect. At the end of your turn, the Digimon with this keyword effect may attack. At the end of the attack, this Digimon is deleted. This effect also allows for attacking an opponent's unsuspended Digimon.
<Execute> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the end of your turn. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
The processing from <Execute> is optional.
The processing from <Execute> for deleting this Digimon at the end of the attack is pending processing. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")
<Progress>
<Progress> is a keyword effect that reads "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent's effects while attacking."
<Progress> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Progress> will activate while the Digimon with this effect is attacking.
<Link +>
<Link +> is a keyword effect that adds the specified number to the maximum link cards of the Digimon with this effect.
<Link +> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

If 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Link +>, the maximum number of link cards will increase according to those numerical values. However, even if a card has multiple instances of <Link +>, the effect isn't considered to be an effect with the combined values from <Link +>. (Examples: If a Digimon has 2 instances of <Link +1>, its maximum number of links will increase by 2, but the Digimon isn't considered to have <Link +2>.)
<Training>

<Training> is a keyword effect that reads "By suspending this Digimon during the main phase, place the top card of your deck at the bottom of this Digimon's digivolution cards. This effect can also activate in the breeding area."
<Training> is an activation-type effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-4 "Activation-Type Effects")

"By suspending this Digimon" in <Training> is an optional processing condition. If this condition is performed, "place the top card of your deck at the bottom of this Digimon's digivolution cards" is mandatory processing.
<Use Req.>
<Use Req.> is a keyword effect that allows a player to ignore the color requirements with the specified cards.
<Use Req.> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
<Use Req.> allows a player to ignore the color requirements with specific Digimon and/or Tamers on the field.
<Ascension>
<Ascension> is a keyword effect. When the card with this effect is deleted, the player may place this card at the top of the security stack.
<Ascension> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect is deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Ascension> is optional.
<Engage>
<Engage> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect may attack at the end of your turn.
<Engage> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the End of Your Turn timing. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
The processing from <Engage> is optional.
<Guard>
<Guard> is a keyword effect. When any of a player's other Digimon would leave the battle area by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, it doesn't leave.
<Guard> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when any of a player's other Digimon would leave the battle area by an opponent's effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
The processing from <Guard> is optional.
<Detach>

<Detach> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon would leave the battle area other than by your effects, by trashing 1 of its specified link cards, it doesn't leave." It is shown on cards using text such as "<Detach ([Seven Code] trait)>."

<Detach> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would leave the battle area other than by its owner's effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
"By trashing 1 of its specified link cards" within <Detach> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "it doesn't leave" will be mandatory.
<Succession>

<Succession> is a keyword effect that reads "This Digimon gains all effects other than <Succession> on its topmost specified digivolution card." It is shown on cards using text such as "<Succession ([Ceresmon])>."
<Succession> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
Rule Checks
Rule Checks
A rule check is a rule for performing the respective processing for certain circumstances during timings when rule checks are possible.
Rule checks aren't performed in the following situations.

Rule checks aren't performed during rule processing. (Examples: If an immediate-type effect activates during rule check processing and a Digimon is played, a rule check won't yet be performed for that Digimon even if it has 0 DP. A rule check will only be performed after the previous rule check is resolved. If the Digimon has 0 DP upon the new rule check, it will then be deleted.

Rule checks aren't performed during effect processing. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Digivolving] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets-3000 DP and <Security Attack-1> until the end of their turn," a Digimon whose DP becomes 0 due to getting-3000 DP will be deleted upon a rule check after it gains <Security A. -1>.)
The respective processing is performed simultaneously for the following circumstances during timings when rule checks are possible.
Deletion Targets
A Digimon placed in the battle area whose DP is 0
Trash Targets
Digimon without DP placed in the battle area
Option cards placed in the battle area (except Option cards placed in the battle area by an effect)
Cards other than Digimon placed in the breeding area (except cards placed in the breeding area by an effect)
Face-down cards placed on the field
Link cards for a Digimon that has exceeded the link limit (only the cards that exceed link limit are trashed)
Link cards that don't meet the link requirements
Linked cards in a card category other than those specified in the notes for <Link>
Other Information
Pending Processing

Pending processing refers to processing for rules or effects that is pending. Pending processing will be processed at the predetermined timing for the corresponding rule or effect, similar to triggered effects. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] Gain 3 memory. Lose 3 memory at the end of the turn," "lose 3 memory at the end of the turn" is pending processing that is processed similar to how it would be processed if it triggered at the end of the turn.)
If other processing will be performed at the same time as pending processing, it is performed similar to effects that trigger simultaneously. For details, refer to 15-4-3 "Simultaneous Triggering")
Overwrite Processing

Overwrite processing refers to when the processing that is normally performed for a rule or effect is overwritten with different processing using "instead" in text. (Example: In an effect that reads "[Main] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less. If you have a Digimon with [Greymon] in its name, instead delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with the lowest DP," the overwrite processing is shown right before "instead."

If overwrite processing is optional, it will be possible to choose to overwrite with the different processing shown for the "instead" in text, and it will be considered optional processing. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] Reveal the top 4 cards of your deck. Add 2 cards with the [Blue Flare] trait among them to the hand. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck in any order. When you have [Kiriha Aonuma], you may return 1 [MetalGreymon] from your trash to your hand instead," while the player has [K iriha Aonuma], they can choose whether or not the processing is replaced with the processing shown for "instead," and they can choose whether or not they return 1 [MetalGreymon] from their trash to the hand.)
If overwrite processing is mandatory, the processing must be overwritten with the different processing shown for the "instead" in text, and it will be considered mandatory processing.

The overwrite processing for immediate-type effects can't be interrupted. (Example: If an effect reads "when any digivolution card would be trashed from another of your Digimon by effects, you may trash a digivolution card from this Digimon instead," it can't be interrupted.
Infinite Loops

An infinite loop refers to a state where a set of processing will continue infinitely or must be continued infinitely as a result of processing for a rule or effect, and game progress is no longer possible.
If an infinite loop occurs and neither player has the ability to stop it, that game ends in a draw.

If an infinite loop occurs and one of the players has the ability to stop it, use the following procedure. After performing the following processing, it will not be possible to perform the actions for the same infinite loop again.
The turn player declares to repeat the processing a certain number of times. If the turn player doesn't have the ability to stop the infinite loop, skip this step and go on to the next step.
The non-turn player declares to repeat the processing a certain number of times. If the non-turn player doesn't have the ability to stop the infinite loop, skip this step and go on to the next step.
The processing is executed at least the number of times that was declared it would be repeated, then the player stops the processing when possible.
